name: Tyran Stokes
video_note:
Overview
Tyran Stokes shows a polished, physical, and versatile offensive game against Pittsburg State. His highlights combine powerful finishes, creative ball handling, rebounding, foul drawing, and underrated passing—traits that suggest he can contribute immediately as a freshman.

The key takeaway is that Stokes does not rely on one scoring method. He creates advantages through strength, size, skill, and decision-making, then either finishes himself or finds teammates when the defense reacts.

Key Points
Stokes uses his strong frame effectively, including a spin move and physical lane finish early in the reel [00:00:00–00:00:05].
His passing stands out as an important secondary skill. He creates an easy Reeves finish after drawing defensive attention [00:00:08–00:00:15; 00:01:18].
He contributes on the glass before converting a right-handed finish for the Jayhawks [00:00:25–00:00:28].
Team ball movement and spacing help create favorable driving opportunities, forcing defenders into difficult closeouts [00:00:33].
Stokes scores in several ways: a backboard finish, free throw, aggressive drive that draws a foul, and later another successful finish [00:00:41–00:00:53; 00:02:24].
His height and high shooting release give him an advantage as a wing, allowing him to get shots off over defenders [00:01:10].
He flashes advanced handle, including a behind-the-back recovery move after losing control of the ball [00:02:10; 00:02:17–00:02:23].
Explanation
Stokes’s value comes from his ability to make multiple kinds of plays. A player who can score only from one area is easier to defend; Stokes can drive, finish through contact, make free throws, use post-related actions, and set up teammates.

His high release point matters because it makes his shot harder to contest. Combined with wing mobility and a sturdy build, it gives him tools to attack smaller defenders physically and challenge taller defenders with skill.

Conclusions and Implications
Stokes looks capable of making an early impact because his game is well-rounded rather than dependent on pure athleticism or one scoring move. The sequence supports the idea that he can function as both a scorer and a playmaker, especially when surrounded by strong spacing and movement.

Additional Notes
The commentary identifies passing as “a real underrated characteristic” of Stokes’s game [00:00:05–00:00:15].
His highlight sequence reinforces the principle that “great offensive players usually can score in multiple ways efficiently” [00:01:51–00:01:59].

name: Jordan Smith Jr.
video_note:
Overview
Arkansas delivered a commanding 98–58 Baha Mar Summer League victory over Carleton, powered by Jordan Smith Jr.’s all-around performance: 20 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists. His scoring, transition playmaking, rebounding, and defensive activity set the tone for a team effort marked by pressure defense and fast-break finishes.

The central takeaway is Smith Jr.’s versatility. He impacted virtually every phase of the game, reinforcing the commentator’s assessment that he brings “energy, defense, and… an attitude of winning” [00:00:14].

Key Points
Smith Jr. started aggressively with athletic finishes and a controlled drive to the basket [00:00:04–00:00:32].
He showed transition ability with a coast-to-coast finish, using his speed and strength to get to the rim [00:00:53].
Defensive takeaways fueled Arkansas’s offense:
Smith Jr. made a steal and found Torrey for a transition finish [00:01:12].
He added another takeaway later, with his open-court movement compared to a running back [00:01:33–00:01:35].
His playmaking stood out through passes that created high-percentage scoring opportunities:
He assisted Bowser on a powerful dunk [00:02:17].
He delivered a pocket pass to J.J. Andrews in transition [00:02:50].
Smith Jr. also made a buzzer-beating three-pointer, extending his impact beyond the paint and transition game [00:01:42–00:01:49].
Arkansas maintained control throughout, closing with a 40-point victory over Carleton [00:03:12–00:03:19].
Explanation
A triple-double means reaching double figures in three statistical categories. Smith Jr. recorded one with points, rebounds, and assists—evidence that he was not simply a scorer, but a player who helped create possessions and scoring chances for teammates.

Arkansas’s defensive pressure created turnovers, which led to fast breaks. This is especially effective because a steal can turn defense into an immediate scoring opportunity before the opposing team has time to set up.

Conclusions and Implications
Smith Jr.’s 20-point, 11-rebound, 11-assist performance demonstrated a complete skill set: finishing, passing, rebounding, defending, and making timely perimeter shots. Arkansas’s 98–58 result also reflected strong team depth, with teammates contributing dunks, deep shots, and transition finishes.

Additional Notes
The source includes a separate quote referring to an earlier 106–59 exhibition win over the Bahamas [00:00:06–00:00:12]; it appears distinct from the reported 98–58 win over Carleton.
A commentator predicted Smith Jr. could record many triple-doubles [00:02:08–00:02:11], an opinion supported by his all-around stat line in this game.

name: Caleb Holt
video_note:
Overview
Caleb Holt stood out during Arizona’s preseason trip to Lithuania because of his all-around impact. He contributed as a scorer, rebounder, passer, and defender, showing that he can affect possessions in several ways rather than relying on one skill.

His most notable moments combined individual creation with team-oriented play: attacking the basket, finding teammates, fighting for offensive rebounds, and helping disrupt opposing attacks.

Key Points
Holt helped stop a Ukrainian offensive possession with strong defensive involvement at 00:01:27.
He scored two points while dealing with foul trouble, recorded as three personal fouls, during the Ukraine sequence at 00:01:37.
An offensive rebound at 00:01:42 demonstrated his effort and activity around the basket.
He attacked the rim against Regimantas at 00:02:41, displaying confidence as a driver.
Holt delivered a pass to Jaruševičius that drew a foul at 00:02:47, highlighting his ability to create opportunities for teammates.
A spin move against Urmanavičius at 00:02:57 showcased his individual ball-handling and finishing skill.
Coach Rimas Kurtinaitis frequently used both players in the game against Estonia at 00:02:03, suggesting a willingness to rely on the group’s depth.
Explanation
Holt’s value comes from versatility. A player who rebounds can extend possessions; one who passes can turn defensive attention into open looks for teammates; and one who defends can prevent easy scoring chances. Holt showed elements of each role in a short stretch of action.

The pass to Jaruševičius is especially meaningful because it reflects decision-making, not just scoring. When defenders collapse on a driver, recognizing the open teammate can be as valuable as finishing the play personally.

Conclusions and Implications
Holt’s preseason performance suggests he can provide Arizona with flexible, two-way production. His combination of rim pressure, playmaking, rebounding effort, and defensive activity gives him multiple ways to contribute even when his own shot is not falling.

Additional Notes
Bryce James also made a long-distance three-pointer at 00:01:06.
The available source does not provide Holt’s full statistical line or enough detail to evaluate his efficiency across the entire tour.

name: Stefan Joksimovic
video_note:
Overview
Stefan Joksimovic drives Slovenia’s success through aggressive scoring, timely defensive plays, and fast-break finishing. Although the footage includes moments against multiple opponents, the central takeaway is consistent: Joksimovic repeatedly turns momentum in Slovenia’s favor, especially when turnovers create transition opportunities.

The tone is energetic and celebratory, emphasizing both Joksimovic’s individual skill and Slovenia’s ability to convert defense into efficient offense.

Key Points
Joksimovic starts efficiently, reaching seven points while shooting 3-for-4 from the field early in the first quarter [00:00:00].
Slovenia uses its final possession of the opening quarter effectively:
A pass produces a strong Krampelj finish [00:00:17].
Joksimovic then drives to the basket with five seconds remaining for a major late-quarter score [00:00:23].
A Slovenian steal creates a crucial breakaway opportunity, with Joksimovic finishing for two points in a potentially game-deciding moment [00:00:34–00:00:42].
Slovenia’s transition attack thrives after defensive stops:
An emphatic block highlights the team’s defensive intensity [00:01:09].
A Czech turnover leads to a rapid break and Joksimovic’s powerful dunk off Horvath’s setup [00:01:21–00:01:27].
Joksimovic also stretches defenses with perimeter shooting, hitting another three-pointer after Jerkovic passes out of a double team [00:01:38–00:01:49].
Another steal produces a “flying finish” from the 17-year-old standout [00:02:03–00:02:12].
In later action, Joksimovic scores through contact, makes a left-handed finish off a screen, and hits a significant step-back shot late in the game [00:02:34, 00:02:59–00:03:08].
Larsson provides Sweden’s major scoring output with 29 points [00:03:16].
Explanation
Slovenia’s best offense comes from transition: forcing a turnover, pushing the ball quickly, and attacking before the defense can set up. The sequence ending in Joksimovic’s dunk is a clear example—one mistake by Czechia immediately becomes an easy, high-energy Slovenian score [00:01:21–00:01:27].

Joksimovic’s value is not limited to one skill. He scores at the rim, shoots from three-point range, creates offense after steals, and performs in late-game situations. This versatility makes him difficult to defend: opponents cannot simply protect the paint or chase him off the three-point line.

Conclusions and Implications
Joksimovic emerges as Slovenia’s defining playmaker in the highlights, combining efficient early scoring with decisive plays in pressure moments. Slovenia’s defensive activity and fast-break execution amplify his impact, turning steals and stops into immediate points.

The footage also shows that Slovenia faces capable opposition, particularly Sweden, where Larsson’s 29-point performance demonstrates the need for Slovenia to maintain its defensive intensity [00:03:16].

Additional Notes
The source contains an apparent age inconsistency: Joksimovic is called a “17-year-old sensation” [00:02:06–00:02:12] but is also described as 25 years old [00:03:20–00:03:25]. The correct age is unclear in source.
Late missed free throws create tension before Slovenia secures a qualifying point through Omic’s made free throw [00:00:50–00:00:54].

name: Bruce Branch III
video_note:
Overview
Bruce Branch III made an impressive unofficial debut as BYU faced Nebraska in an exhibition at the Marriott Center in Provo. In a game marked by momentum swings and a physical, fast-paced finish, Branch contributed as a scorer, rebounder, and playmaker.

The clearest takeaway is that Branch’s value went beyond his scoring. His smooth shooting, court vision, transition play, and activity on both ends helped BYU secure the win, 72–61 [00:03:37].

Key Points
BYU entered the exhibition with an almost entirely rebuilt roster; Rob Wright III was identified as the primary returning exception [00:00:17].
Branch scored his first BYU points by following his own miss, showing effort around the basket [00:00:27].
His shooting profile stood out: he was credited with shooting 42% from three-point range, combining volume with efficiency [00:00:41].
Branch displayed playmaking ability with a notable one-handed pass that set up a forceful dunk [00:01:17].
After a turnover, he quickly pushed offense forward and found Koller inside for an early basket [00:01:31].
His unofficial debut line was 15 points, 6 rebounds, and 5 assists, reflecting broad impact rather than a one-dimensional performance.
BYU’s victory came in a tightly contested, “boxing match”-like game with continuous action [00:03:43].
Explanation
Branch’s performance matters because a new roster needs players who can fill multiple roles. Scoring is valuable, but his rebounds helped finish possessions and his assists created efficient shots for teammates. His ability to move from defense to offense quickly also fit BYU’s transition opportunities.

The one-handed pass and alley-oop sequence illustrated more than athletic flair: they showed vision and confidence in making difficult reads under pressure [00:01:23]. His three-point shooting adds another layer, forcing defenses to respect him on the perimeter.

Conclusions and Implications
Branch’s debut suggested he could become a versatile contributor for BYU. He paired efficient shooting with playmaking and effort plays, giving the Cougars options in both half-court and transition offense.

BYU’s exhibition win over Nebraska also offered an encouraging early sign for a roster undergoing major turnover. Branch’s ability to contribute across categories may be especially important as the team builds chemistry.

Additional Notes
The game’s highlights included several other BYU contributors, including Rob Wright III, Chandler, Koller, and Eason.
Some names and scoring details in the source are inconsistent, including references to “Bruce Brown III” and an apparent score error. The supported final score is 72–61 [00:03:37]

name: Anthony Thompson
video_note:
Summary

Anthony Thompson appears as a primary offensive option and a vocal leader on the floor. He shows a versatile scoring package, willingness to attack closeouts, and confidence in late-clock situations. Defensively he competes consistently, though occasional lapses in positioning appear during transition. Overall, he impacts the game on both ends and is a clear go-to player for his team.
Offensive strengths

Scoring versatility: Uses dribble penetration, pull-up midrange jumpers, and finishes at the rim. Comfortable scoring off the bounce and in isolation sequences.
Ball handling under pressure: Keeps control when defenders apply pressure on the perimeter, able to create space with change-of-pace and crossover moves.
Aggressiveness on drives: Attacks gaps decisively, often forcing help defenders and creating opportunities for teammates.
Shot confidence: Willing to take contested shots and step into catch-and-shoot opportunities; shows belief in his shot mechanics.
Playmaking from the ball screen: Recognizes and exploits ball-screen actions—either splitting screens, pulling up, or kicking out to open shooters.
Situational decision-making: Chooses between finishing himself and finding open teammates rather than forcing low-percentage plays; shows good court awareness in late-clock situations.
Free-throw aggression (when fouled): Seeks contact and gets to the line, demonstrating a desire to draw fouls in scoring opportunities.
Offensive areas to improve

Shot selection consistency: Occasionally opts for contested midrange or long two-point shots when better passing options exist; could be more selective when the defense collapses.
Three-point volume/efficiency: Not a high-volume or highly efficient 3-point shooter in this game; extending range and improving catch-and-shoot percentage would make him more difficult to defend.
Left-hand finishing: Shows stronger finishing on his dominant side; left-hand finishes and layups can be developed for better balance around the rim.
Tempo control: In certain possessions, his quick drives can get ahead of the offense, reducing teammates’ opportunities to find spacing; working on pacing the offense and drawing defense before penetrating would increase team efficiency.
Defensive strengths

On-ball intensity: Plays with energy on the ball, applying pressure to primary ball-handlers and contesting shots when matched up.
Help defense instincts: Senses when to rotate and provide help in the paint; communicates with teammates and participates in team defensive schemes.
Rebounding effort: Shows willingness to box out and pursue rebounds, especially on the defensive glass.
Competitiveness: Plays with urgency and effort—doesn’t shy away from physical matchups and contested plays.
Defensive areas to improve

Pick-and-roll coverage: Can be caught over-committing on hedges or going under screens at times, which leads to open looks or mismatches; improving on-screen navigation and communication would reduce these breakdowns.
Transition awareness: Occasionally late to locate an opponent in fast-break situations, which can allow easy scoring opportunities for the other team.
Fouling/discipline: Shows moments of reaching or ill-timed contests that result in fouls; refining timing and footwork could decrease foul trouble and free-throw opportunities for opponents.
Playmaking and basketball IQ

Vision and passing: Demonstrates solid court vision—finds cutters and open shooters after drawing defenders. Effective in short-pocket passes and timely kick-outs.
Decision-making under pressure: Generally makes sound reads against varying defenses; rarely forces risky passes in traffic.
Leadership: Acts like a team leader—directs teammates, stays engaged in both ends, and makes plays that lift team performance.
Adaptability: Adjusts to defensive schemes, using counters like step-backs, pull-ups, and changes of speed to keep defenders off balance.
Physical profile and conditioning

Athleticism: Shows quickness, explosiveness off the bounce, and ability to finish through contact—plays with good burst in short areas.
Frame and strength: Appears to have a solid youth frame for his age group; can absorb contact but could benefit from strength training to finish more consistently against taller/stronger defenders.
Stamina: Maintains intensity for extended stretches and is active late in the game, suggesting good conditioning for tournament play.
Mental makeup and intangibles

Competitiveness: High motor and desire to win; plays hard on both offense and defense.
Poise: Remains calm in late-game situations and takes on decision-making responsibilities.
Coachability: Responds to in-game adjustments and communicates with teammates—appears receptive to direction.
Confidence: High confidence level, sometimes stepping into difficult shots and plays under pressure.
Coachable points and development plan

Improve three-point shooting: Implement a regimented shooting program emphasizing mechanics, catch-and-shoot reps, and off-the-dribble threes to extend his threat range.
Strength and finishing: Off-season strength and conditioning focused on lower-body power and upper-body strength will help him finish through contact and absorb screens.
Left-hand work: Daily reps on finishing with non-dominant hand, including layups, floaters, and contact finishes to become more two-sided at the rim.
Pick-and-roll defense drills: Work on communication and footwork for hedge/contain decisions and practice switching vs. staying home to lower pick-and-roll breakdowns.
Decision-making under pressure: Simulate late-clock and double-team scenarios in practice to refine reads, pass choices, and when to pull up versus kick out.
Conditioning for transition defense: Drills emphasizing sprint-back defense, locating shooters, and transition communication will reduce easy opponent transition points.
Film review: Study tendencies of defenders and referees to improve shot selection and draw fouls smartly rather than through unnecessary contact.
Tendencies and scouting tags

Tendencies: Attacks closeouts, prefers driving to the right off the bounce, frequently pulls up in midrange when defense drops, looks for kick-outs after collapsing defense.
Scouting tags: Primary ball-handler, go-to scorer, clutch-minded, midrange pull-up, penetrator-and-pass, high-motor defender.
How opponents should game-plan for him

Force him to his weaker side and make him use his left hand more; take away midrange pull-ups with physical closeouts and make him pass.
Use disciplined on-ball pressure and smart help rotation to limit straight-line drives and challenge his finish at the rim.
Hit open shooters early when he draws help; force him to be the facilitator rather than the primary scorer.
Test his three-point consistency by switching defenders and putting versatile wing defenders on him to contest perimeter shots.
Bottom line Anthony Thompson is a dynamic, confident lead guard with the scoring ability and playmaking vision to control games at this level. He impacts both ends through aggressive drives, smart passes, and active defense. With focused work on three-point efficiency, ambidextrous finishing, pick-and-roll defense, and added strength, he projects as a high-upside prospect who can expand his scoring range and durability while maintaining his leadership role.

name: Quentin Coleman
video_note:
Overview

Position/Build: Wing-forward (primary small forward/power forward mix). Listed around 6'4 with a strong, compact frame that plays bigger than his height.
Role/Usage: High-activity two-way connector who initiates offense off drives and offensive rebounds and functions as a secondary playmaker. Often the engine of his team on both ends, drawing attention inside and creating opportunities for teammates.
Motor & Intangibles: Exceptional effort and competitiveness. Consistently pursues loose balls and offensive rebounds, shows late-game poise, and competes on every possession. Plays with high basketball IQ — understands spacing, when to attack, and when to kick. Defensive communication and willingness to take charges are pluses.
Offense — Strengths

Drive and finish: Aggressive attacking instincts. Uses strong shoulders and lower-body leverage to get into the paint off the dribble and finishes through contact, often converting on putbacks and plays off the glass.
Post toughness: Comfortable operating with his back to the basket in short-roll/post area; uses angles, footwork and physicality to create space for layups or quick turnarounds.
Rebounding/second-chance scoring: Elite rebounder for his size at the U18 level. Secures offensive rebounds proactively and converts many into immediate putbacks or kick-outs, creating extra possessions.
Passing & decision-making: Adequate passer for a wing — recognizes help-side rotations, finds open shooters after drawing double teams, and makes timely skip and drop passes. Shows vision in closeout/pressure situations to exploit rotating defenders.
Mid-range scoring: Effective pull-up game off the dribble and turnaround jumpers from mid-range. Uses change-of-pace and shoulder fakes to gain separation.
Spot-up shooting: Shows capability to knock down spot-up triples but needs consistency. Has made some catch-and-shoot attempts; shooting mechanics are workable though not yet fully reliable as a primary floor-spacing trait.
Pace & control: Comfortable pushing in transition and equally effective in half-court sets where he can attack downhill or operate in pick-and-roll/pick-and-pop actions.
Offense — Areas to Improve

Three-point consistency: While he can step out and attempt threes, his long-range shot percentage and consistency need improvement to become a true floor spacer, especially defending bigger matchups at higher levels.
Shot selection under pressure: Occasionally forces tough contested shots when double-teamed rather than always opting to reset or move the ball quickly.
Ball-handling in tight spaces: Good overall, but would benefit from tighter handles to better navigate trapping defenses and create more separation for pull-ups or drives on quicker wings.
Defense — Strengths

Rebounding & positioning: Strong rebounder from the wing; uses anticipation and physicality to grab contested boards and initiate transition.
On-ball effort & help defense: Active on-ball defender who applies pressure and uses length and strength to bother ball-handlers. Willing and effective in the help role, contesting shots and rotating quickly.
Defensive IQ: Reads screens and rotations well; demonstrates awareness of when to hedge, when to drop, and when to recover. Plays passing lanes opportunistically for deflections and turnovers.
Competes vs. bigger opponents: Despite being undersized for some matchups, he uses strength and leverage to battle post-ups and deter easy interior touches.
Defense — Areas to Improve

Lateral quickness vs elite wings: May struggle to stay in front of the quickest, most explosive perimeter scorers; needs to refine footwork and possibly improve conditioning/speed to better guard chase-downs.
Closeout discipline: At times allows shooters a step on catch-and-shoot situations when closing out too upright; needs to be lower and more controlled in closeouts to contest without fouling.
Physical & Athletic Profile

Strength: Plays stronger than his frame suggests; uses compact build to absorb contact and finish through bodies.
Mobility: Adequate mobility — quick first step into the lane, solid verticality on finishes and rebounds. Not an elite leaper but times his jumps well.
Endurance: High stamina and plays with consistent energy across minutes; functions well in high-tempo schemes.
Playstyle & Fit

Best fit: Versatile frontcourt wing in schemes that value physical, high-effort defenders who can rebound and generate offense close to the rim. Ideal in college systems that emphasize ball movement and that will allow him to attack off closeouts and operate in pick-and-roll or short-roll actions.
Offensive role possibilities: Secondary initiator, short-roll/pop screener who can slip, offensive rebounder/finisher and occasional shooter. Can run the floor in transition and finish lobs or interior kickouts.
Defensive role possibilities: Tough perimeter and help defender on switches, rebounder who secures possessions and sparks offense; fits well as a switchable forward on many lineups at the collegiate level.
Projection

Near-term (college): Immediate high-impact role expected as a rebounder, interior finisher and glue defender. Will contribute minutes early due to motor, toughness and decision-making.
Long-term (pro potential): With improved perimeter shooting and lateral quickness, projects as a versatile 3-and-D forward capable of guarding multiple positions and spacing the floor. Without those upgrades, projects as a high-level collegiate starter and complementary pro piece who excels in transition, defense and rebounding.
Summary Quentin Coleman is a high-motor, physical wing who plays bigger than his size. He combines strong rebounding, interior finishing and solid passing vision with competitive defense and excellent effort. The primary growth areas are consistent perimeter shooting and quicker lateral mobility. As he refines those skills he should comfortably transition into a major collegiate role and has the tools to develop into a versatile two-way player at higher levels.

name: Colben Landrew
video_note:
Overview: Colben Landrew is a modern scoring wing with a strong perimeter offense, good pace in transition, and developing playmaking instincts. At the FIBA U18 Americup he showcased reliable catch-and-shoot ability from deep, the willingness and competence to attack in transition, and competent off-ball movement. His skill set projects as a multi-positional floor spacer who can also initiate actions off pick-and-rolls occasionally and create downhill opportunities in transition. Defensively he shows effort and the ability to contest shots but needs improvement on consistent on-ball strength and defensive awareness in help rotations.

Strengths

Spot-up shooting: Converts at a high clip from beyond the arc for the age group (video notes 42.9% on threes during the competition). Quick release, good shooting mechanics from the catch and from short kick-outs off drives. Comfortable shooting from corner and wing.
Off-ball movement: Reads the floor and finds space, times cuts and relocations well. Gets open through simple but effective movement, which maximizes his catch-and-shoot effectiveness.
Transition & pace: Recognizes offensive transition, runs the floor intelligently, and finishes or pulls up from distance. Good timing on streaking threes and makes the right decisions on the break.
Shot creation in rhythm: Shows the ability to create his own looks off dribble-jumps and pull-up threes. Comfortable attacking closeouts and pulling up rather than forcing contested long twos.
Passing instincts: Makes timely passes, particularly in read-and-react sequences following penetration or kick-outs. Capable of hit-and-run delivery to streaking teammates; shows vision to swing the ball quickly.
Competitiveness: Plays with energy, pressures defenses with active movement and requires attention from opponents—can change defensive schemes because of his perimeter threat.
Areas for development

Strength and finishing through contact: Will benefit from added functional strength to absorb contact on drives and finish through bodies in traffic at the collegiate/pro level.
Creating off the dribble against length: While effective in youth competition, needs refinement when facing longer, more physical defenders—improve hesitations, change-of-pace, and counters to consistently break down NBA-caliber on-ball defenders.
Playmaking consistency: Shows flashes of passing, but needs to develop an advanced playmaker’s toolkit—dribble combos, pocket passing under pressure, and the ability to run offense when primary ball-handlers are stifled.
Defensive awareness and consistency: Active hands and effort are present, yet he can be late on rotations or beaten on drives if overcommitting. Strengthening closeout technique, footwork, and communication will raise his overall defensive impact.
Rebounding: Will need to improve boxing out and aggressive pursuit of rebounds to maximize value as a 3-and-D wing at higher levels.
Basketball IQ & Intangibles

Reads defensive positioning well; uses opponent tendencies to find spot-up opportunities.
Disciplined in spacing and doesn’t force iso possessions often; prefers to operate within team actions.
Demonstrates coachability: shows a willingness to defer, make the extra pass, and play within the team scheme.
Competitive motor: consistently engaged on both ends; appears to take pride in defensive contesting and transition effort.
Fit and Projection

College fit: Immediate fit as a perimeter spacer and secondary ball-handler for programs valuing shooting, pace, and off-ball movement. Can carve out minutes early as a 3-and-D wing while adding strength and defensive polish.
Role projection: Likely a high-volume catch-and-shoot wing with secondary playmaking duties initially. With added strength and improved on-ball creation, could evolve into a primary perimeter scorer and more versatile two-way wing.
Long-term ceiling: Solid collegiate starter and rotation player; potential high-level pro prospect if shot creation, strength, and defensive consistency are developed. Best long-term role is as a multi-positional wing who spaces the floor, moves well without the ball, and can take over games offensively in rhythm.
Skill breakdown (1–10)

3PT shooting: 8 — mechanics and percentage in competition indicate real shooting skill.
Mid-range/pull-up: 6 — capable but not a primary weapon; effective off closeouts and in transition.
Ball-handling: 6 — sufficient to create space; needs more advanced moves to consistently beat defenders.
Passing/vision: 6 — solid passer in motion offense and transition; needs growth as a pick-and-roll initiator.
Finishing at rim: 6 — able in open court; needs strength and craft in traffic.
Defense (on-ball): 6 — active and competitive; must improve strength, lateral quickness under pressure, and rotation timing.
Rebounding: 5 — average for position; can improve with effort and technique.
Basketball IQ: 7 — reads game well and makes sound decisions.
Recommendations for development

Strength & conditioning: Implement a targeted program focusing on lower-body and core strength to improve finishing through contact and defensive anchoring, while preserving explosiveness.
Shooting volume & range: Continue high-volume, game-situation shooting drills (catch-and-shoot, pull-up threes, off-screens) and incorporate contested shooting to translate to higher levels.
Ball-handling drills: Add advanced two-ball and live-dribble combos, plus counter moves to beat longer defenders and create for others.
Defensive footwork & IQ: Intensive closeout, slide, and recovery drills; film study focused on rotations and positioning to cut down on late help and blown coverages.
Playmaking under pressure: Situational drills where he must read help defense, make quick pocket passes, and initiate gravity-creating actions against live resistance.
Strengthen finishing: Post-up/drive finishing drills against physical defenders and using contact finishes (underarm, off-arm, floaters) to increase efficiency in close quarters.
Summary assessment Colben Landrew projects as an impactful perimeter scorer with legitimate three-point stroke, strong transition instincts, and promising secondary playmaking ability. With added strength, improved on-ball creation against length, and more consistent defensive fundamentals, he can become a reliable two-way wing and a high-value college contributor. Short-term ceiling: immediate rotation player and floor spacer. Long-term upside: primary perimeter scoring wing and multi-positional defender if development plan is executed.

name: Luigi Suigo
video_note:
Overview Luigi Suigo is a physically imposing wing prospect who has developed noticeably in strength, endurance, and scoring consistency during the 2025–26 season with KK Mega Basket. He projects as a multi-positional wing capable of impacting the game on both ends through outside shooting, transition scoring, and improving defensive play. His combination of size, shooting touch, and willingness to run the floor makes him an intriguing NBA Draft candidate.

Measurements & Physical Profile

Position: Wing (SF/PF tweener depending on matchup)
Frame: Strong, muscular build for a young wing; uses size effectively on drives and when finishing through contact
Athleticism: Above-average straight-line speed and good stamina; not an elite leaper but explosive enough to finish in transition and on put-backs
Mobility: Adequate lateral quickness for his size; can chase smaller wings but may struggle versus ultra-quick guards in space
Offensive Skillset

Shooting: Reliable catch-and-shoot three-point threat with range. Displays a quick release and confidence in taking deep shots, often stretching the defense and creating driving lanes for teammates.
Spot-up scoring: Very effective as a spot-up shooter off ball movement and skip passes. Cleans up possessions with timely threes that swing momentum.
Pull-up game: Has a developing pull-up jumper from mid-range and short three; still inconsistent but shows potential as a creating shooter when defenders close space.
Finishing: Strong at the rim when attacking off drives or in transition, capable of using size to finish through contact and score on put-backs.
Ball-handling & playmaking: Not a primary playmaker. Handles adequately in transition and on simple pick-and-roll reads; makes the right pass in half-court settings and shows solid court awareness. Can deliver sharp, timely passes in high-speed sequences.
Decision-making: Generally calm under pressure; picks spots to shoot and looks to return quickly to defense after scoring plays.
Defensive Skillset

Perimeter defense: Competent on-ball defender against average wings; uses physicality to bother opponents and contest outside shots. Can be vulnerable to sudden direction changes by top-tier quick guards.
Help and rotations: Shows good defensive instincts in team schemes — hustles back after offensive plays, contests shots, and participates in help-side rotations.
Rebounding: Active on the glass for a wing; secures defensive rebounds and initiates transition offense.
Defensive upside: With continued improvement in lateral quickness and footwork, his size and strength project well to guard multiple positions.
Intangibles & Motor

Energy: High work rate and consistent effort both in transition and on the defensive end. Frequently hustles for loose balls and rebounds.
Competitiveness: Plays with a confident, composed demeanor; shows willingness to take big shots in key moments.
Basketball IQ: Understands spacing and team concepts; makes smart plays rather than forcing offense.
Conditioning: Excellent endurance, able to maintain effectiveness late into games.
Role Projection & Fit

Short term: 3-and-D wing role in modern systems — spot-up shooting, transition scoring, defensive versatility on the wing, and hustle plays.
Long term: With improved ball-handling and lateral quickness, could expand into a secondary creator who initiates offense in specific lineups and defends multiple positions. Fits best in systems that value spacing, pace, and switching defense.
Team fit: Ideal for teams needing wing shooting and physicality on the perimeter. Valuable in pick-and-pop schemes, pace-and-space offenses, and lineups that emphasize defensive switching.
Strengths

Consistent catch-and-shoot three-point ability with deep range
Strong frame enables finishing through contact and securing rebounds
High endurance and transition scoring threat
Good off-ball movement and timing for spot-up opportunities
Calm decision-making and reliable hustle plays
Areas for Improvement

Ball-handling and creating shots consistently off the dribble
Lateral quickness and footwork to handle elite perimeter players
Playmaking vision under pressure to become a more consistent secondary creator
Defensive discipline in isolation situations against smaller, quicker guards
Summary Luigi Suigo is a physically mature wing prospect with a proven ability to shoot from distance, score in transition, and contribute on defense and the glass. His steady improvement in strength and endurance combined with reliable long-range shooting make him a strong candidate for a 3-and-D role at the next level. With targeted development on ball skills and lateral mobility, he could expand his offensive repertoire and increase his defensive versatility, raising his floor and ceiling as a professional prospect.

name: Braylon Mullins
video_note:
Overview Braylon Mullins is a dynamic two-way wing with scoring versatility, playmaking instincts, and impact defensive ability. He combines advanced ball-handling and finishing skills with a reliable perimeter shot, making him a consistent threat in multiple offensive actions. Defensively he shows strong anticipation, shot-contesting ability, and the physicality to guard multiple positions. His poise in late-game situations and ability to finish in traffic elevate his floor-to-floor value.

Strengths

Scoring Versatility: Can score from all three levels — pull-up midrange, catch-and-shoot threes, and finishes at the rim using runners, floaters, and aggressive drives. Comfortable creating his own shot and off-hand finishes in traffic.
Shot Creation: Uses quick change-of-pace dribbles, step-backs and ball fakes to create space for jumpers. Shows the ability to shoot off screens and on the move, keeping defenders honest.
Off-ball Movement: Constantly moving without the ball, cutting to the rim and using back-cuts and flare actions effectively. This movement generates easy looks for himself and teammates.
Playmaking: Good vision for a wing; finds cutters and reads closeouts to deliver timely passes. Can run transition and make the right read on the break.
Clutch Composure: Demonstrates calm and confidence in late-game situations, capable of making game-deciding shots under pressure.
Defensive Instincts: Anticipates passing lanes and creates turnovers. Shows toughness in contesting shots and provides help defense that results in blocks and altered attempts.
Basketball IQ: Makes smart plays, understands spacing and situational needs, and adapts to defensive coverages (e.g., attacking zones or exploiting switching schemes).
Areas for Improvement

Consistency from deep: While he can knock down big threes, his long-range percentage can fluctuate game-to-game; improved shot selection and a more consistent release would raise his floor.
Strength and finishing through contact: Effective at finishing, but could add more upper-body strength to absorb contact and convert at a higher rate against physical defenders in the paint.
Turnover management: Aggressive playmaking can sometimes lead to forced or risky passes; a more measured approach in certain possessions would limit giveaways.
Defensive discipline on switches: Versatile defender but can be exploited on prolonged switches by bigger, stronger opponents or crafty ball-handlers; improved footwork and leverage in those matchups would help.
Role & Fit

Primary scoring wing in lineups that ask him to create off the dribble and attack closeouts.
Secondary ball-handler/playmaker in motion offenses and transition, facilitating for cutters and shooters.
Switchable perimeter defender in schemes that value versatility and help-side rotation.
High-leverage option late in games for isolation or pick-and-roll actions where his ability to shoot and finish can decide outcomes.
Key Tendencies

Prefers to attack off the dribble into a midrange or floater when primary driving lane is threatened.
Often curls or flare-screens to create catch-and-shoot opportunities; comfortable spotting up and firing quickly.
Frequently cuts hard to the basket when defenders’ attention is on the ball, creating easy interior looks or drawing fouls.
Looks to create downhill on transition; pushes the pace when he reads an unsettled defense.
On defense, he reads passing lanes aggressively and will gamble for steals and charges when the opportunity arises.
Projection

Immediate contributor at the collegiate or professional level as a two-way wing who can score in isolation, spot up from three, and defend multiple positions.
With improved three-point consistency and added strength, he projects as a starting-caliber wing who can handle late-game responsibilities and be a primary perimeter defender.
Summary Braylon Mullins is a confident, multi-dimensional wing whose scoring toolkit and defensive instincts make him a valuable impact player. He can create and convert in high-pressure moments while also contributing as a playmaker and versatile defender. With marginal improvements in strength, shot consistency, and turnover discipline, his upside moves from high-impact role player to reliable go-to wing.

name: Thomas Haugh
video_note:
Overview

Versatile forward who blends inside physicality with perimeter skill. Strong motor and competitive mentality; impacts the game on both ends. Reliable contributor in late-game situations and March pressure environments.
Physical Profile

Size and Strength: Above-average length and solid frame for a college forward; uses body effectively to seal defenders and absorb contact. Not an elite athlete but plays stronger than metrics suggest.
Mobility: Adequate lateral quickness for his position. Moves well in short bursts, allowing him to attack closeouts and cut effectively.
Conditioning and Effort: High activity level—plays hard for 40 minutes, chases loose balls, and pursues offensive rebounds consistently.
Offensive Skillset

Scoring Inside: Comfortable finishing through contact around the rim. Uses a variety of short-range moves (hook/loop shots, up-and-under) and converts off the glass in traffic. Good feel for spacing and timing on post entries.
Mid-Range and Perimeter Shooting: Has a serviceable three-point stroke and can hit from beyond the arc, giving him floor-spacing value. Not a volume deep threat, but enough range to pull opposing bigs out of the paint.
Free-Throw Tendency: Draws fouls frequently thanks to aggressive drives and physical finishing. Converts at the line enough to be a reliable late-game asset.
Playmaking: Shows the ability to make simple, decisive passes—effective on slips, pick-and-roll reads, and short-range kickouts. Not a primary creator off the dribble but makes the right play in ball-movement schemes.
Off-Ball Movement: Reads defenses well, makes timely cuts, and finds scoring opportunities via slips and backdoor actions. Good chemistry with perimeter teammates and timely offensive rebounds that lead to second-chance points.
Defensive Profile

Paint Protection and Interior Defense: Uses size and length to deter easy inside looks. Takes good defensive angles and contests shots without always fouling. Effective in help rotations and rim deterrence.
Perimeter Defense: Can be challenged by quicker, smaller wings on switches but maintains position and uses reach to disrupt shots and passing lanes. On-ball defense vs. guards can be situational; best defended with help or when matched with similarly sized opponents.
Rebounding: Active on both ends—brings hustle and timing to both offensive and defensive boards. Not solely reliant on vertical explosiveness; uses positioning and anticipation to secure rebounds.
Defensive IQ: Smart, disciplined defender who communicates and rotates well. Makes hustle plays—loose ball recoveries, contested outlet passes.
Tendencies and Intangibles

Aggressiveness: Plays with physicality and a competitive edge. Will attack mismatches and seek contact to earn trips to the line.
Basketball IQ: Reads game situations, executes coachable plays (slips, screens, rotations) and rarely forces low-percentage actions. Good decision-making in late-game scenarios.
Leadership and Poise: Composed under pressure; performs in big moments. Brings energy that elevates teammates, especially on hustle plays and defensive stands.
Fit and Projection

Best Role: High-minute starting forward or primary backup big in systems that value space-and-craft—pick-and-roll/pop actions, slip-and-fill schemes, and inside-out offense. Fits well in teams that emphasize toughness, rebounding, and halfcourt execution.
NBA/Next-Level Projection: Floor-spacing forward with finishing ability and defensive versatility. Upside hinges on continued perimeter shooting consistency, lateral mobility to guard quicker wings, and incremental playmaking development.
Areas for Improvement: Consistency from three-point range and catch-and-shoot scenarios; lateral quickness and footwork to improve switchability on defense; increased ball-handling to create more off-the-dribble offense.
Summary Thomas Haugh provides an impactful mix of interior scoring, physical finishing, and complementary perimeter shooting. He defends the paint effectively, rebounds with effort, and contributes smart, team-oriented playmaking. With continued development of shooting consistency and lateral agility, he projects as a valuable two-way forward in schemes that require toughness, spacing, and reliable finishing.

name: Jason Crowe Jr.
video_note:
Overview Jason Crowe Jr. is a high-level, five-star guard with elite scoring instincts and a well-rounded offensive arsenal. He combines advanced ball-handling, high-level finishing, and consistent outside shooting with strong competitive instincts and poise in late-game situations. He projects as a primary ball-handler and primary scorer at the collegiate level with strong upside as a two-way playmaker.

Physical Profile

Height/Frame: Prototypical guard size for high-major college programs; wiry but strong enough to absorb contact and finish through traffic. Shows good balance and lower-body strength on drives and contact finishes.
Athleticism: Explosive first step and above-average short-area quickness. Strong leaper for his size which aids in finishing at the rim and contesting shots on defense.
Motor: High competitive motor; consistently seeks the ball and impacts the game on both ends. Plays with urgency and a desire to finish.
Offensive Skillset

Shot Creation: Elite. Generates offense for himself off the bounce and with step-backs, jab-step pull-ups, change-of-pace moves and creative finishes (euro-steps, floaters, spin moves). Comfortable creating separation against closeouts and in isolation.
Shooting Range & Mechanics: Reliable catch-and-shoot three-point range and capable of converting pull-up threes off screens or step-backs. Mechanics are repeatable; shows confidence to take open looks and contested long-range attempts when needed.
Finishing: Excellent around the rim. Uses body control, angles, and a variety of finishes (power dunking, tough layups through contact, floaters) to consistently convert in traffic. Shows touch on runners and floater off the dribble.
Passing & Playmaking: Good vision and passing feel for a primary scorer. Makes timely reads, hits teammates in rhythm when defenses collapse, and can run pick-and-roll actions effectively. Not a traditional distributor but a capable secondary playmaker.
Ball Handling: Advanced for his age. Tight crossover, hesitation dribble, and change-of-direction moves allow him to beat defenders off the dribble and into scoring opportunities or to create passing lanes.
Shot Selection & Efficiency: Aggressive but efficient — capable of long scoring runs without forcing poor shots. Converts a variety of shots at a high clip due to good decision-making and finishing ability.
Defensive Profile

On-Ball Defense: Competitive and engaged. Uses quick hands and anticipation to disrupt passing lanes and force turnovers. Can hold his own on the perimeter due to quick lateral feet and effort.
Off-Ball Defense: Solid understanding of help principles; recovers well after contests. Can be prone to occasional mental lapses in positioning but generally reliable.
Rebounding & Hustle Plays: Active rebounder for his position, especially on the defensive end. Will go after loose balls and contributes in transition opportunities off defensive stops.
Intangibles

Clutch & Mental Makeup: Calm and confident in late-game situations; demonstrated the ability to take and make the game-deciding plays. Competes at a high level in pressure moments and shows leadership by example.
Work Ethic & Coachability: Appears to be a hard worker with a growth mindset; makes adjustments mid-game and shows polish beyond his age.
Competitiveness: High — attacks every matchup and thrives when challenged.
Areas for Improvement

Consistency in playmaking volume: Can expand his assist numbers by further improving reads in accelerated collegiate defenses and trusting playmaking instincts on the move.
Defensive consistency vs. more physical/longer guards: Needs to refine technique and leverage to handle exceptionally long or physically stronger guards at the next level.
Turnover management in heavy usage: When carrying an offensive load, he sometimes risks turnovers; tightening ball security in traffic will boost overall efficiency.
Projection Short term (college): Immediate high-usage scoring guard and primary offensive option. Will contribute early with instant scoring in transition, pick-and-roll, and isolation sets while developing into a more complete playmaker.
Long term (pro potential): Projects as a two-way scoring guard with starter-level scoring ability and developing playmaking. With continued improvement in shot selection, defensive consistency, and playmaking, he has the upside to be an above-average combo guard at the next level and a potential primary scoring option.

Summary Jason Crowe Jr. is a dynamic scorer with advanced finishing skills, reliable shooting, and confident late-game decision-making. He brings toughness, creativity, and a competitive mindset that translate well to higher levels of play. Continued growth as a playmaker and defensive consistency will elevate him from an elite high school scorer to a full-time two-way lead guard at the collegiate and professional levels.

name: Cameron Williams
video_note:
Overview

Position: Wing (shooting guard / small forward)
Strengths: Elite catch-and-shoot three-point shooting, consistent off-ball movement, poise in late-game situations, solid scoring instincts.
Areas to improve: Limited creation off the dribble, finishing through contact, defensive consistency against quicker wings.
Prospect profile: Floor-spacing wing who thrives in motion offenses and as a spot-up threat. Projects as a 3-and-D complementary piece at higher levels if defensive quickness and on-ball fundamentals are developed.
Offensive Skillset

Shooting: Primary skill. Demonstrates reliable three-point stroke from multiple spots beyond the arc. Accurate catch-and-shoot mechanics and quick release allow him to convert off ball screens and in transition. Shows the ability to hit corner threes and pull-up triples when given space.
Off-ball movement: Reads defensive rotations well and uses cuts, flare screens, and pindowns to get open. Consistently finds pockets in the defense, which maximizes his shooting opportunities.
Shot selection: Generally disciplined; prefers open looks and capitalizes on team actions that generate clean shots. Shows good restraint, not forcing difficult pull-ups or contested shots often.
Ball-handling and creation: More of a secondary creator. Dribble creation is a relative weakness — limited ability to create off the bounce against tight closeouts. Best suited coming off screens or receiving passes in rhythm.
Finishing: Solid at catch-and-shoot layups and transition finishes. Needs improvement finishing through contact in half-court drives; can struggle against longer, physical defenders near the rim.
Playmaking: Not primary playmaker. Makes the simple pass and can hit the roll or slip when defenders over-commit. Value as a weak-side cutter and as a passer in ball movement sequences.
Defensive Profile

On-ball defending: Adequate but inconsistent. Can stay with average wings in spot minutes, but can get beat by quicker guards in isolation. Needs improvement in lateral quickness and footwork to consistently defend ball-handlers.
Off-ball defense and awareness: Reasonably aware; shows willingness to rotate and contest perimeter shots. Must avoid gambling on steals which can lead to blown coverages.
Rebounding: Provides modest help on the glass for a wing. Uses positioning and effort to secure defensive rebounds but not a dominant rebounder.
Defensive upside: With focused development on technique, anticipation, and strength, he can be a reliable rotational defender on the wing — especially in schemes that emphasize switching and team help.
Physical and Athletic Traits

Size: Typical wing size for college/pro level; enough length to contest shots and be a switchable defender in many matchups.
Athleticism: Above-average straight-line explosiveness for transition and spot finishes. Lateral quickness is average, which impacts on-ball defense and ability to create off the dribble.
Conditioning and motor: Plays with consistent energy on offense, shows competitive desire when engaged. Needs to maintain focus defensively throughout games.
Intangibles

Composure: Displays poise in clutch moments; comfortable taking and making big shots. Crowd reactions indicate confidence under pressure.
Basketball IQ: Reads team actions well and picks spots to shoot. Makes smart movement without the ball and understands spacing.
Competitiveness and demeanor: Confident scorer who feeds off momentum. Works within team concepts and benefits from structured offensive systems.
Role Projection

Short term: High-value rotation player as a catch-and-shoot specialist who spaces the floor and moves well without the ball. Effective in transition and as part of pick-and-pop or off-ball screening schemes.
Long term: With improvements in ball-handling and defense, projects as a multi-positional wing who contributes both offensively as a reliable three-point threat and defensively in switch-heavy schemes. Best fit on teams that prioritize ball movement and spacing.
Development Priorities

Improve lateral quickness and on-ball defensive footwork to contain quicker guards and be a dependable switch defender.
Enhance shot-creation skills — ball-handling drills, change-of-pace moves, and finishing through contact to expand scoring beyond spot-up threes.
Add strength to better absorb contact when attacking the rim and to hold position on defense and rebounding.
Continue to refine catch-and-shoot mechanics while adding a consistent mid-range pull-up to diversify offensive arsenal.
Work on playmaking instincts for occasional secondary-creation duties (dribble hand-offs, short drives and paint reads).
Summary Cameron Williams is a high-IQ wing with a strong specialty as a catch-and-shoot three-point scorer and smart off-ball mover. He brings instant floor spacing and late-game calm, making him a valuable complimentary piece. His ceiling depends on improvements in defensive quickness and creation off the dribble, but as-is he projects as a dependable 3-and-D role player in structured offensive systems.

name: Dylan Mingo
video_note:
Overview Dylan Mingo stood out as the primary offensive engine in his camp game, showing a blend of aggressive scoring, advanced playmaking, and competitive toughness. He looks comfortable initiating offense and imposing his will downhill, creating for himself and teammates in halfcourt sets and transition.

Strengths

Aggressive scoring: Consistently attacks the rim with a downhill dribble, using body control and contact balance to finish or draw fouls.
Playmaking: Can run the offense and create high-quality looks for teammates off drives, kick-outs, and pick-and-roll actions. Sees the floor and times passes well in transition and crowded paint situations.
Midrange/floater package: Uses pull-up jumpers and floaters to counter shot-blockers and avoid turnovers when space is limited.
Ball handling under pressure: Maintains control against full-court and on-ball pressure, navigating traps and initiating counters to free teammates.
Competitiveness and toughness: Plays with a high motor; not afraid to take responsibility late in possessions and absorb contact to finish or get to the line.
Tempo control: Knows when to push in transition and when to slow the offense to run sets or find the best shot.
Areas for Improvement

Three-point consistency: Shows range but needs more reliable catch-and-shoot and off-the-dribble three-point shooting to consistently stretch defenses and punish ball-screen hedges.
Decision-making in traffic: Aggression sometimes leads to forced or risky passes that result in turnovers; improving patience and passing angles in tight windows will increase offensive efficiency.
Perimeter lateral quickness: Can be vulnerable vs. very shifty, low-center-of-gravity guards on the perimeter; quicker defensive slides and anticipation will help him contain those matchups.
Shot selection refinement: Occasionally settles for contested midrange or long twos rather than working for cleaner attempts or driving to create better kick-outs.
Physical & Athletic Profile

Frame and strength: Strong enough to finish through contact and absorb physical play. Handles contact well when attacking the rim.
Explosiveness: Good downhill burst to separate from slower defenders; adequate verticality to finish above the rim when attacking the paint.
Conditioning: Shows the stamina to maintain aggression across the game, initiating offense and defending with consistent intensity.
Playstyle & Fit

Projection: Fits as a lead guard or primary scoring guard at the next level. Best in uptempo systems that allow for transition opportunities and pick-and-roll-heavy sets where he can read and react.
Role fit: Ideal as a ball-dominant guard who can close games, initiate pick-and-rolls, and create offense for teammates. Also effective as a secondary creator in lineups that need a downhill penetration threat.
Intangibles

Leadership: Commands the floor with confidence; willing to take key shots and direct teammates.
Coachability: Responds to coaching during the game, adjusts tempo and reads according to scheme.
Competitive instinct: High desire to win possessions and impact the game on both ends.
Summary & Projection Dylan Mingo projects as a high-upside primary ball-handler and scorer who can create for himself and others. If he develops more consistent long-range shooting and tightens decision-making in heavy traffic, he can become a reliable two-way lead guard at the collegiate level and beyond. Teams seeking an assertive playmaker who thrives in transition and pick-and-roll action should consider him a strong fit.

name: Baba Oladotun
video_note:
Overview
Five-star 2026 recruit who committed to Maryland over Georgetown, Kentucky and Arkansas. Ranked No. 10 overall in the Class of 2026 by 247Sports. Late-blooming jumbo wing whose footwork and ball skills are the most praised parts of his game. Status: incoming freshman, no college games yet.

Strengths (inference from published scouting)
Three-level scoring, including rising over defenders with touch.
Footwork, which 247Sports analyst Adam Finkelstein cited as where he stands out most.
Size and length: listed at 6-10 with a reported 7-1 wingspan.
Pedigree: USA Basketball junior programmes since 2023, and a finalist for the 2026 Team USA U18 squad.

Areas for Improvement (inference from published scouting)
Consistency: his 2025-26 season was cut short, so there is little recent playing time to judge.
Physical development: still growing into his frame, which matters against bigger wings in the Big Ten.
Injuries: an ankle injury sidelined him early in 2025-26. One source also says he tore an ACL in December 2025, but that page mixes up other players, so it is unverified.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-10 on the Maryland roster (other sources say 6-8 and 6-9). Weight 195 lbs. Wingspan 7-1. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a versatile wing who can operate on the perimeter and attack from mid-range. Whether he becomes a point-forward or a wing scorer depends on how his handle and decision-making develop.

Intangibles
Maryland native who chose a programme close to family. Came through Kevin Durant’s Team Durant AAU programme. An AAU coach described strong basketball instincts from an early age.

Summary and Projection
One of the highest-rated freshmen in the 2026 class, with a high ceiling if his size and skills translate. Any projection depends on his first season at Maryland.

Sources: Maryland roster (umterps.com); CBS Sports and Sports Illustrated recruiting coverage; High School on SI; Hoopshq.

name: Tounde Yessoufou
video_note:
Overview
2025 consensus top-20 recruit and McDonald’s All-American. Productive freshman season at Baylor, scoring 17.8 points a game on 46.5% shooting, and widely described as a projected NBA lottery prospect. School note: some sources list him at St. John’s for 2026-27 and others still list Baylor, so check before using.

Minutes 32.6, points 17.8, rebounds 5.9, assists 1.6, steals 2.0, blocks 0.6, turnovers 1.9.
Field goal 46.5%, three-point 29.3%, free throw 74.6%.
Season highs: 37 points against BYU, 27 against Colorado.

Strengths (based on verified stats)
Scoring volume: 17.8 points on 46.5% shooting is productive for a freshman.
Defensive activity: 2.0 steals and 0.6 blocks a game suggest active hands and length.
Rebounding: 5.9 a game is strong for his listed position.

Areas for Improvement (based on verified stats)
Three-point shooting: 29.3% is below what is usually needed from a primary wing scorer.
Turnovers: 1.9 a game against 1.6 assists is a low ratio for a player expected to create.
Free throws: 74.6% is solid but not elite.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-5, weight 215 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Scores at all three levels and rebounds well for his size, so projects as a wing who can play both ends. The key questions are three-point percentage and turnovers.

Intangibles
No verified information beyond his recruiting profile and reported community work.

Summary and Projection
Strong freshman campaign on the numbers. If his three-point percentage improves and his turnovers come down, he fits a lottery-level wing profile.

Sources: ESPN player page; RotoWire game logs; lines.com; Stat Sniper; Wikipedia.

name: Stefan Vaaks
video_note:
Overview
Estonian guard, born May 2005, who played one season at Providence in 2025-26 and has committed to Illinois for 2026-27, keeping three years of eligibility. Estonian League champion in 2025 and a Big East All-Freshman Team selection in 2026. Before college he played for BC Kalev in the Latvia-Estonia league.

Current Stats (2025-26 Providence, 31 games, per game)
Minutes 31.4, points 15.8, rebounds 2.5, assists 3.2, steals 0.8, blocks 0.3.
Field goal 40.3%, three-point 35.0%, free throw 83.9%.
Missed time with a pre-season knee surgery, an undisclosed injury, and an illness.

Strengths (based on verified stats)
Shooting: 35.0% from three on high volume makes him a real perimeter threat.
Scoring: 15.8 points a game as a freshman, including a 26-point game against Marquette.
Free throws: 83.9% is strong.

Areas for Improvement (based on verified stats)
Efficiency: 40.3% from the field is below what is usually expected from a primary scorer.
Size: listed at 6-6 or 6-7 with a light build (190 to 212 lbs), which could be tested by bigger college guards.
Availability: several missed games across the season.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-6 to 6-7, weight 190 to 212 lbs (sources differ). No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a combo guard who scores and makes shots from distance. His assist numbers suggest he can handle some playmaking.

Intangibles
Competed for Estonia’s national team. Head coach Kim English said Providence chose him after watching film and meeting him, citing his skill set and willingness to attack.

Summary and Projection
A productive freshman who could develop into a reliable scorer at Illinois. The main questions are field-goal efficiency and whether his health holds.

Sources: Providence roster and athletics releases; RotoWire; lines.com; Wikipedia.

name: Toni Bryant
video_note:

6-9 power forward from Tampa, Florida. McDonald’s All-American and ESPN 100 recruit, ranked as high as No. 14 nationally. Signed with Missouri in September 2025.

Works effectively from the post, turning back-to-the-basket possessions into face-up attempts.
Mid-range catch-and-shoot ability, described as unusual for a big.

Rim protection, with 6.5 blocks a game as a junior.

Three-point shooting: a scouting writer says he will be serviceable at best, and his college numbers don’t exist yet.
Level of competition: his high school production is not a guide to how he will handle college bigs.
Physical development: his frame changed over the off-season, so consistency is still being established.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-9, weight 215 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a power forward who scores facing up and from mid-range and works away from the ball. Whether that translates to a ball-screen-heavy college offence is the main test.

Intangibles
No verified information beyond his background and family, as listed on the Missouri roster.

Summary and Projection
One of the more established 2026 prospects by recruiting ranking and high school production. Shooting and rebounding at college level are the key questions.

name: Billy Richmond
video_note:

Arkansas sophomore from Memphis, Tennessee, and a four-star Memphis East prospect. He declared for the 2026 NBA Draft, was projected by On3 as a No. 36 pick, then withdrew and returned to Arkansas for 2026-27.

Around 11 points, 4 rebounds and 2 assists a game. Sources differ slightly (points 10.0 to 11.2, rebounds 4.0 to 5.4), so treat these as approximate.

Strengths (inference from published scouting)
Versatile guard-forward hybrid who can drive to the basket.
Reliable mid-range jumper.
Aggressive defender who uses size to guard multiple positions.

Three-point shooting: shooting volume and efficiency from three are limited in the verified logs.
Consistency: his scoring varies a lot from game to game.
Ankle: he left a game with an ankle issue during 2025-26, though he returned.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Listed at 6-6 (some sources say 6-4), 205 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a wing who can guard multiple positions and create offence off the dribble. His NBA draft interest suggests his size and defence are the main draw.

Intangibles
Chose to return to school, and head coach John Calipari said he was excited by Richmond’s mentality of “let’s do something special.”

Summary and Projection
A useful sophomore with a versatile skill set rather than a standout scorer. Improved three-point shooting would give him a clearer role.

Sources: On3; Stat Sniper; RotoWire; lines.com; ProBallers.

name: Bryson Howard
video_note:
Overview
Five-star 2026 recruit who committed to Duke over North Carolina and Kentucky. Son of former NBA All-Star Josh Howard. Ranked No. 1 in Texas and No. 12 nationally by the 247Sports composite. Status: incoming freshman, no college games yet.

Current Stats (2025-26 high school, Heritage HS, Frisco TX, senior season)
22.8 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 3.2 steals, 1.3 blocks a game. This comes from the Gatorade Texas Player of the Year release, which also names the team as a 5A state champion. Other reports say Heritage reached the state semifinals, so treat the championship claim as unconfirmed.
Junior season: 17.1 points and 10.2 rebounds over 37 games.
2026-27 college: season not started.

Strengths (inference from published scouting)
Shooting: Duke head coach Jon Scheyer called him one of the premier shooters in the country.
Versatility: can play on and off the ball and defend multiple positions, per Scheyer.
Finishing: described as a versatile finisher who is almost unstoppable when he gets downhill and catches around the basket.

Areas for Improvement (inference from published scouting)
Level of competition: his production is from high school, so college scoring and shooting efficiency are untested.
Ball-handling and creating: the published scouting focuses on shooting and finishing, with less on creating for others.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-5, weight 185 to 190 lbs, wingspan reported at 6-11. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a wing who can shoot, finish and guard multiple positions. Scheyer says Duke’s pace fits his game.

Intangibles
Gatorade-listed 3.95 weighted GPA. Has volunteered for years with The Josh Howard Foundation, serving meals and packing care packages.

Summary and Projection
One of the top 2026 wings, and a shooter with a complete-looking high school profile. Whether the shooting translates against college defences is the key question.

Sources: Duke athletics announcement (goduke.com); Gatorade Texas Player of the Year; Sports Illustrated Duke coverage; The Ticket; Field Level Media.

name: Shelton Henderson
video_note:

Five-star 2025 recruit who originally committed to Duke, backed off, and signed with Miami in April 2025. 247Sports ranked him No. 25 overall in his class. Status: sophomore in 2026-27, after a freshman season at Miami.

Minutes 30.8, points 13.7, rebounds 4.8, assists 2.0, steals 1.1, blocks 0.4.
Field goal 56.3%, three-point 27.1%, free throw 58.8%.

Finishing: field goal percentage over 56% reflects efficient shot selection near the rim.
Defence: 1.1 steals a game and described as a solid defender who guards multiple perimeter positions.
Downhill attacks: described as best when attacking downhill and finishing at the rim.

Three-point shooting: 27.1% is a clear weakness, and published scouting says he needs to improve as a perimeter shooter to be a rotation piece in the NBA.
Free throws: 58.8% is low.
Consistency: he scored under 19 points in every game during his first month before a breakout.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-6 (DraftVision and Lines), weight 240 lbs. Described as strong and physical, though not elite vertically.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a physical two-way wing whose value comes from slashing, toughness and defensive versatility, rather than as a primary creator.

Intangibles
Said his game is about being versatile. Scouts describe him as a team player who fits within ball movement and spacing.

Summary and Projection
A productive freshman who could be a valuable physical wing. Improving the three-point shot and free throws would make him a more complete player.

name: Patrick Ngongba II
video_note:

Duke sophomore centre from Manassas, Virginia. Former five-star recruit who came through Paul VI Catholic High School. Status: sophomore, with a bigger role expected in 2026-27.

Projects as a rim-protecting centre with passing ability who may fit a modern, spaced-out frontcourt.

Son of a George Mason women’s basketball assistant. No further verified information.

A useful big whose production should increase with a bigger role. Whether his offence grows beyond finishing and passing will decide his projection.

name: Deron Rippey Jr.
video_note:
Overview
Five-star 2026 point guard from Brooklyn, New York, who committed to Duke over NC State, Miami, Tennessee and Texas. Ranked No. 1 point guard in the 2026 class by the 247Sports composite. Status: freshman in 2026-27, and he has already played his first Duke game.

2025-26 high school (Blair Academy, NJ, senior season): 15.7 points, 6.3 assists, 5.3 rebounds, 2.0 steals a game. Gatorade New Jersey Player of the Year. Team went 30-2.

2026-27 college, first game vs. Belmont: 11 points, 2 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 steal in 22 minutes.

Defence: described as a menacing defender with elite athleticism and the ability to set the tone on that end.
Athleticism: explosive in transition and half-court, uses burst to reach the rim and finish with authority.
Court vision and feel: described as a true floor general who can initiate the offence, with strong passing and IQ.

Shooting: scouts say he is still refining his offensive skill set and needs his shooting to take a step forward.
Size: listed at 6-1 or 6-2 and 175 to 185 lbs, which matters against bigger guards in the ACC.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-2 (Gatorade and CBS) or 6-1 (Rivals), weight 180 to 185 lbs. Explosive athletic profile, per scouts. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a lead guard who can defend, run an offence and finish in transition. His first Duke game suggests he will be used as a floor general from day one.

Intangibles
Described by Gatorade as inspiring confidence in teammates. Has volunteered with a toy drive and food kitchen near his home in Brooklyn.

Summary and Projection
One of the best point guards in the 2026 class by ranking. The main questions are shooting and how his size holds up in the ACC.

Sources: Gatorade New Jersey Player of the Year; CBS Sports; On3 Rivals; SI; Field Level Media; Duke athletics coverage.

name: Trey McKenney
video_note:

Flint, Michigan, native and McDonald’s All-American who was Michigan’s Mr. Basketball. Freshman in 2025-26 and part of the Michigan team that won the 2026 national championship. Status: sophomore in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 freshman season, Michigan, 34 games)
Minutes 21.6, points 9.6 (some sources list 9.9), rebounds 2.6, assists 0.9, steals 0.4, blocks 0.0.
Field goal 44.6%, three-point 37.6%, free throw 91.3%.
Made 12 threes in the NCAA Tournament, including a key shot in the national championship game against UConn.
Season high: 16 points in one game.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Shooting: 37.6% from three and 91.3% from the line show a reliable shooter.
Scoring: described as able to score from all three levels and to create his own shot.
Defence: described as a strong defender with a physical frame.

Playmaking: 0.9 assists a game is low for a guard, though scouts describe him as an underrated initiator.
Role: he came off the bench for much of the year, so his production as a starter is not yet proven.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-4, weight 225 lbs. Described as having a strong frame and physical play style. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a combo guard who can score off the dribble, shoot from distance and defend. His role is set to grow in 2026-27 after the departure of Michigan’s starting backcourt.

Intangibles
Son of a Flint family with a basketball legacy: his aunt was Flint’s first female professional player. Captain of his high school team, and described as mature beyond his years.

Summary and Projection
A high-calibre shooter who will have a bigger role as a sophomore. Improving playmaking and proving he can start would define his projection.

Sources: Michigan athletics roster; RotoWire; ESPN; Lines; UMHoops.

name: Christian Collins
video_note:
Overview
Five-star 2026 forward from St. John Bosco High School in Bellflower, California. McDonald’s All-American and a Naismith All-American Underclassman Honourable Mention. Ranked No. 5 in ESPN’s SCNEXT Top 100 and No. 5 overall on the 247Sports composite at one point. Committed to USC. Status: incoming freshman, no college games yet.

Current Stats (2025-26 high school, senior season)
26.1 points, 9.6 rebounds, 3.5 assists a game, per the USC roster bio. He also averaged 17.6 points and 9.7 rebounds across his junior and senior seasons.
Sources conflict on one figure: USC’s bio also gives 12.0 points and 9.7 rebounds for 2025-26, so check which season that line refers to.
2025 Nike EYBL (summer circuit): 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 2.8 turnovers, 41.9% from the field, 21.2% from three on 2.4 attempts.
2026-27 college: season not started.

Strengths (inference from published scouting)
Athleticism: good athlete and transition finisher who gets up well at the rim, including a quick second jump.
Ball-handling and creating: good foundation as a ball-handler with dribble-drive ability.
Length: listed with a 7-1 wingspan. Gets low and moves his feet well on the perimeter.
Motor: described as vocal and consistently playing hard.

Areas for Improvement (inference from published scouting and verified stats)
Three-point shooting: scouts call him a poor shooter from three, and his EYBL 21.2% was very low.
Efficiency: his EYBL shooting and turnover numbers show games where production and efficiency drop off.
Shot: one scouting report describes his shot as unorthodox and flat, and questions whether it extends to college and NBA range.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height listed at 6-8 (NBADraft), 6-9 (USC) and 6-8 to 6-9 elsewhere. Weight 200 lbs. Wingspan 7-1 (NBADraft). No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a versatile forward who attacks the rim and creates in transition. His shooting development will decide whether he fits a modern wing-forward role.

Intangibles
Described as vocal and a hard worker. Played for USA Basketball junior teams and the 2026 Nike Hoop Summit. Scouts rate his leadership and intangibles highly.

Summary and Projection
One of the most talented freshmen in the 2026 class by athleticism and length. The main question is whether his shooting develops enough to make his game consistent.

Sources: USC roster; NBADraft.net; ESPN; RealGM; SI; Field Level Media.

name: Bryson Tiller
video_note:

Atlanta native and four-star 2025 recruit who came through Pace Academy and Overtime Elite. Redshirted at Kansas, then played one season there in 2025-26 before transferring to Missouri for 2026-27. Points 7.9, rebounds 6.1, assists 1.0 (35 total), blocks 1.3 (45 total).

Rim protection: 1.3 blocks a game as a starter.
