Height 6-11 (Kansas and AP), though other listings say 6-8 to 6-10. Weight 210 to 240 lbs, depending on the source. Wingspan 7-3 (Kansas). No verified testing data.

Projects as a traditional big who protects the rim and rebounds. Missouri will want him to be a more active offensive piece.

Intangibles
Son of former NFL player Tony Tiller and has two younger siblings. Also has a family background in Atlanta basketball, and played for the Overtime Elite programme.

A solid rim protector and rebounder with a role-player profile. Improving his offence and shooting would decide whether he becomes a starter at Missouri.

name: Brandon McCoy Jr.
video_note:

Build: listed at 6-5 but under 200 lbs, so he may struggle with physicality.
Health: a right-knee ACL injury will keep him out for the 2026-27 season.

Height 6-5, weight 200 lbs. No verified testing data.

Projects as a two-way guard who can score and defend. The injury means his fit at Michigan will be unknown until 2027-28.

Respectfully asks for “junior” to be used in references. Has represented USA Basketball, winning gold at the 2024 FIBA U17 World Cup and 2025 FIBA U19 World Cup.

One of the most decorated guards of the 2026 class on paper, but the ACL injury means his college career will start late. The ranking and USA Basketball record are verified, and his college impact is not yet known.

name: Amare Bynum

Four-star 2025 recruit from Omaha, Nebraska, who played his high school senior year at Link Academy. Ohio State’s roster lists him at 6-8 and 240 lbs. Status: sophomore in 2026-27 after a freshman season at Ohio State.

Efficiency: 50.2% from the field as a freshman.

Three-point shooting: 31.8% is below what is needed from a frontcourt player on the perimeter.

Height 6-8, weight 240 lbs (Ohio State roster). No verified testing data.

Projects as a physical frontcourt player who can rebound and finish, with a jump shot that could expand his role. With Bruce Thornton gone, he is expected to take on more scoring.

His father, Omar Bynum, played four seasons at Iowa State (2000-03). No further verified information.

A good freshman with a clear base in rebounding and efficiency. Developing his perimeter defence and three-point shot would decide whether he becomes a top frontcourt player in the Big Ten.

name: Ivan Kharchenkov
video_note:

German forward from Munich who came through Bayern Munich. He won the 2025 Bundesliga title with Bayern and played 23 EuroLeague games in 2024-25. He joined Arizona as a freshman in 2025-26 and was a regular starter. Status: sophomore in 2026-27, returning to Arizona.

Current Stats (2025-26 freshman season, Arizona)
Points 10.4, rebounds 4.3, assists 2.3, steals 1.4 a game, in 39 appearances. ESPN lists 21 games and 21 starts, so check the appearance count.
Field goal 49 to 51%, three-point 31.5 to 31.7%, free throw 72 to 75%.
Minutes about 28 a game.
Season high: 26 points against Memphis in a Hoops HQ-noted game.

Efficiency: about 50% from the field for a freshman guard-forward.
Playmaking: 2.3 assists a game, with a season-high of 8 assists in one game.
Defence: 1.4 steals a game and a season-high five steals against Alabama, which Arizona called a first for a true freshman against a Top 25 opponent.

Three-point shooting: about 31.5% is below what is needed for a primary wing.
Turnovers: about 1.5 a game is high relative to his assists.
Free throws: 72 to 75% is only average.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-7 (Arizona), with other listings at 6-7 and 2.01 m. Weight 230 lbs (Arizona roster). No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a versatile forward who can play across the frontcourt and handle some playmaking. His European experience and size make him a good fit for a switchable role.

Intangibles
Played in the Bundesliga and EuroLeague before joining Arizona. Named the first true freshman to post five steals against a Top 25 opponent in the 2025-26 season.

Summary and Projection
A productive, efficient freshman with international pedigree. Improving his three-point shooting and reducing turnovers would make him a more complete player.

Sources: Arizona athletics roster; ESPN; RotoWire; Lines; HoopsHQ; PHNX Sports.

name: Dame Sarr

International guard from Duke’s 2025 class, described by CBS as one of basketball’s top international prospects. Played his freshman season at Duke in 2025-26 and was a regular starter for part of it. Status: sophomore in 2026-27.

Height listed at 6-8 (Stat Sniper, Rotowire) and 6-6 in some other listings, weight 190 lbs. No verified testing data.

Projects as a wing-guard who can shoot, defend and rebound for his size. His role is unclear until Duke’s 2026-27 rotation is set.

Duke was described as his dream school. No further verified information.

A useful, long guard who showed flashes but was inconsistent as a freshman. Consistent shooting and better efficiency would define his development.

name: Tyler Tanner
video_note:

Brentwood, Tennessee, native and Gatorade Tennessee Player of the Year. Sophomore at Vanderbilt in 2025-26 (not a freshman, as some listings say). Current Stats (2025-26 Vanderbilt, sophomore season, 36 games)
Points 19.5, assists 5.1, rebounds 3.6, steals 2.4, blocks 0.3.
Field goal 49%, three-point 37%, free throw 85%.
Minutes about 33 a game.
Set Vanderbilt single-season records for assists (184) and steals (86).
Season high: 37 points against Oklahoma.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Scoring: 19.5 a game as a sophomore at 49% from the field.
Playmaking: 5.1 assists a game, and scouts describe him as a primary creator.
Defence: 2.4 steals a game and an SEC All-Defensive Team selection.
Shooting: 37% from three, and 85% at the line.

Size: measured at 5-10 3/4 and 167 lbs at the NBA combine, which is small for a point guard.
Consistency: some of his efficiency depends on tempo, and his shooting numbers at the combine (67.5% in shooting drills) were slightly lower than the college numbers.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 5-10 3/4 (combine measurement), 6-0 (Vanderbilt listing). Weight 167 lbs (combine), 175 lbs (Vanderbilt). No verified athletic testing data beyond the combine shooting drills.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a primary creator who can steer an offence and score off movement. Scouts compare him to Chris Paul, Kyrie Irving and Ty Lawson, and he may start as a sixth man before becoming a starter.

Intangibles
Parents both played basketball at Rice. Described as a true competitor who makes the players around him better.

Summary and Projection
One of the most productive guards in the SEC in 2025-26. His size is the main concern, and the 2026-27 status needs to be confirmed.

Sources: Vanderbilt athletics; RealGM; Proballers; NBA.com draft profile; Nashville Post; Lines; Rotowire.

name: Miikka Muurinen

Height listed as 6-11 (Arkansas), 7-0 (Rotowire) or 6-10 (Duke interest reports). Weight 200 to 215 lbs. No verified testing data.

A talented, large forward with international experience but little verified production. Projection depends on how quickly he adapts to college play in his first season.

Sources: Arkansas athletics roster and signing release; Euroleague.net; RotoWire; Bebasket; Field Level Media; Inside The Hall.

name: Alex Wilkins

name: Amari Allen

Summary and Projection
A high-IQ, productive freshman with a strong rebounding profile. Shooting efficiency and scoring consistency will shape how he develops at Alabama.

Sources: Alabama athletics roster; NBA.com draft profile; RotoWire; ProBallers; WVUA 23; CBS Sports via On3.

name: David Punch
video_note:
Overview
Harker Heights, Texas, native and 2024 high school recruit ranked about No. 100 by ESPN. He developed from a bench forward at TCU into one of the Big 12’s better rebounders in 2025-26, earning honourable mention All-Big 12. He signed with Texas in April 2026. Status: junior in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 TCU, sophomore season, 34 games)
Points 14.1, rebounds 6.8, assists 2.0, blocks 1.9, steals 1.3.
Minutes about 30 a game.
Field goal 50.3%, three-point 23.9%, free throw 65.3%.
Reached double figures in scoring 26 times and had five double-doubles.
Season high: 26 points, seven rebounds and four blocks against Oklahoma State in the Big 12 Tournament.
Freshman season (2024-25): 6.5 points and 4.4 rebounds in 32 games.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Rebounding and rim protection: 6.8 rebounds and 1.9 blocks a game as a sophomore.
Size and versatility: 6-7, 246 lbs, with defensive versatility.
Efficiency: 50.3% from the field is solid for a forward.
Motor: his rebounding and defensive numbers rose sharply in one year.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)
Three-point shooting: 23.9% is the biggest concern. Scouts say he will need to improve as a perimeter shooter to earn an NBA spot.
Free throws: 65.3% is low.
Turnovers: 1.7 a game is high for his assist total.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-7, weight 246 lbs (Texas roster). No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a physical power forward who rebounds and defends. Texas will need him to add shooting range to fit a modern frontcourt.

Intangibles
Son of David Punch Sr. and Felisha Provost. Described by TCU coverage as a key catalyst for the team’s success.

Summary and Projection
A productive, physical forward who turned into a rebounding force in one season. His shooting range will decide his next step.

Sources: Texas athletics; TCU roster; RotoWire; ESPN; Stat Sniper; SI.

name: Alijah Arenas
video_note:
Overview
Son of former NBA All-Star Gilbert Arenas, and a five-star 2025 recruit who reclassified from 2026. He was USC’s highest-ranked commit since Isaiah Collier in 2023. Freshman in 2025-26, and a projected top pick by some mock drafts. He announced a return to USC for 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 USC, 14 games)
Points 14.1, rebounds 2.9, assists 2.1, steals 0.9, blocks 0.5.
Minutes about 28 a game.
Field goal 34.1%, three-point 21.3%, free throw 79.2%.
He missed the first two months of the season after knee surgery, so the sample is short.
Freshman of the Week in February 2026, after scoring 20-plus points in consecutive games. Season high: 29 points in a win over USC’s rivals.

Strengths (inference from published scouting and verified stats)
Scoring: 20-plus points in several games once healthy, and described as a phenomenal scorer by coach Eric Musselman.
Size for a guard: listed at 6-6 to 6-7 with a 199 lb frame.
Pedigree: 29.5 points a game in his high school senior year (2024-25), and one of California’s all-time leading high school scorers.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Shooting efficiency: 34.1% from the field and 21.3% from three are both very low.
Availability: knee surgery and a serious car accident in spring 2025 limited his preparation and his season.
Turnovers: his games often came with several turnovers, so decision-making needs work.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-6 (USC roster) and 6-7 (other sources). Weight 199 lbs. No verified testing data. Recovery from knee surgery and the 2025 accident are the main physical questions.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a scoring guard who can create his own shot. Eric Musselman will expect him to be a primary offensive piece in 2026-27.

Intangibles
Grew up around basketball, with a father who was a three-time All-Star, and uncles who are former NBA champions. Teammates and coaches have praised his work ethic.

Summary and Projection
A high-ceiling scorer with a lot to prove after an injury-affected freshman year. His efficiency and health in 2026-27 will decide his projection.

Sources: USC roster; CBS Sports; Rotowire; Lines; SI; Larry Brown Sports.

name: Juke Harris
video_note:
Overview
Chicago-born or Salisbury, North Carolina native (sources differ) and Second Team All-ACC selection at Wake Forest in 2025-26. Transferred to Tennessee in May 2026 after declaring for the NBA Draft and then returning to college. Tennessee lists him as a junior with two seasons of eligibility.

Current Stats (2025-26 Wake Forest, 35 to 38 games)
Points 21.3 to 21.8, rebounds 6.3 to 6.5, assists 1.6 to 1.9, steals 1.4 to 1.5, blocks 0.4.
Field goal 44.9%, three-point 31.4%, free throw 78.6%.
Minutes about 33.5 a game.
Season high: 38 points against Boston College (12 of 19 from the field, six three-pointers).
Had the largest scoring increase in the country from 2024-25 to 2025-26, going from about 6 points to over 20.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Scoring volume: over 21 points a game as a sophomore.
Rebounding: 6 to 7 rebounds a game from the guard position.
Scoring range: scouts describe him as an explosive scorer who can take over games.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Efficiency: 44.9% from the field and 31.4% from three is below what is expected from a high-volume scorer.
Playmaking: only 1.6 assists a game.
Turnovers: about 2 a game is high.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-7 (Tennessee and Stat Sniper) or 6-5 (older listings), weight 200 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a combo guard who can score in bunches and rebound from the perimeter. At Tennessee, he will be a primary scoring option under Rick Barnes.

Intangibles
Described by Tennessee’s Rick Barnes as explosive and humble, with a good family background.

Summary and Projection
A high-volume scorer who improved a lot in one year. Efficiency and playmaking are the two areas to watch as he takes on a bigger role at Tennessee.

Sources: University of Tennessee athletics; RotoWire; ESPN; Stat Sniper; Wake Forest roster.

name: Ikenna Alozie
video_note:
Overview
Lagos, Nigeria native from Dream City Christian in Glendale, Arizona. Four to five-star 2026 recruit, ranked No. 6 point guard nationally by on3/Rivals and a consensus top-20 prospect. Signed with Houston in November 2025. Status: freshman in 2026-27, with four years of eligibility.

Current Stats
No college games yet.
2024-25 Utah Prospects (summer circuit): 15.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 44.6% from the field, 29 steals in 20 games.
Summer 2025 Peach Jam (first three games): 11.7 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists.
2025-26 high school (Dream City Christian): not verified.
2026-27 college: season not started.

Strengths (inference from published scouting)
Athleticism: described by Houston as highly explosive and strong and well built.
Toughness: Kelvin Sampson’s staff describe him as tough with an old-school mentality.
Scoring at all three levels: described by Rivals as scoring from all three levels, including dunks in traffic.
Defence: named as one of his main strengths by scouts, and he has been described as a tough defensive assignment.

Areas for Improvement (inference from published scouting)
Physical adjustment: 247Sports analyst Adam Finkelstein says he will need time to adjust to the physicality of college basketball.
Ball skills: Finkelstein says his untapped upside depends on continued progress in ball skills and the nuances of the point guard position.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height listed at 6-2 (Houston) to 6-4 (some scouting reports). Weight 180 to 185 lbs. Described as strong and athletic. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a lead guard or combo guard who can score in transition and in the half court. Houston’s system will ask him to run the point.

Intangibles
Described as having an old-school players mentality and being no-nonsense off the court. He chose Houston over Alabama, Arizona, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisville and others.

Summary and Projection
A top-20 guard prospect who is physically ready for college, with his point guard skills the main development area. Projection depends on how his ball-handling and decision-making translate at Houston.

Sources: University of Houston athletics; Rivals; SI; Zagsblog; Field Level Media; Sportskeeda.

name: Malachi Moreno
video_note:
Overview
Georgetown, Kentucky native and 2025 McDonald’s All-American and Kentucky’s Mr. Basketball. Ranked No. 25 in the 2025 class by 247Sports. Freshman in 2025-26 and an SEC All-Freshman Team selection. He declared for the 2026 NBA Draft but kept his college eligibility and announced he would return to Kentucky if he stayed in college.

Current Stats (2025-26 Kentucky, freshman season, 26 games, 20 starts)
Points 7.8 to 8.4, rebounds 6.3 to 6.6, assists 1.7, steals 0.6, blocks 1.5 to 1.7.
Field goal 58.2 to 58.8%, free throw 69.1%.
Minutes about 22 a game.
Led Kentucky in rebounding and blocks, with three double-doubles.
Season high: 17 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists and 4 steals against Mississippi State.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Efficiency: 58% from the field as a freshman.
Rim protection: 1.5 blocks a game in 22 minutes.
Rebounding: 6.3 a game led the team, and he was on the SEC All-Freshman Team.
Defensive upside: described by SI as having enough upside as a defender to earn a spot in the draft.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Free throws: 69.1% is below what is needed from a regular big.
Offence: 7.8 to 8.4 points a game, with no three-point attempts to speak of.
Playmaking: 1.7 assists a game is limited.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 7-0, weight 243 to 250 lbs (NBA profile and Herald-Leader). No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a rim-protecting centre who rebounds and defends, with limited offence so far. His fit will depend on whether he can develop a reliable shot and free throw.

Intangibles
Older brother Michael played at Eastern Kentucky. Credited by coach Mark Pope as one of the season’s highlights for his early growth.

Summary and Projection
A productive, efficient freshman centre whose defence is his calling card. Improving his free throws and adding some offence would be the next step.

Sources: Kentucky athletics roster; NBA.com draft profile; Rotowire; ESPN; Lexington Herald-Leader; SI.

name: Alex Condon
video_note:
Overview
Perth, Australia native and graduate of the BA Centre of Excellence/NBA Global Academy. Florida’s starting forward on the 2025 NCAA champion team and a 2025 All-SEC third team selection. Tested the NBA Draft after his sophomore year, then returned to Florida for his junior season. He announced he will return for his senior season in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Florida, junior season, 34 games)
Points 15.0 to 15.1, rebounds 7.5 to 7.6, assists 3.5 to 3.6, blocks 1.3 to 1.4.
Field goal 55.6%, career-best shooting and rebounding averages.
Averaged 19.3 points over the final 10 games.
Season high: 26 points in a win over a conference opponent.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Efficiency: 55.6% from the field is strong for a forward.
Playmaking: 3.6 assists a game as a 6-11 forward, which is unusual. Florida’s record shows he is one of few Florida players 6-9 or taller to reach 100 assists in a season.
Rebounding and rim protection: 7.5 rebounds and 1.4 blocks a game.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Consistency: he scored 19-plus in only five of his first 25 games, and a late-season ankle injury hurt his numbers.
Three-point range: there is no verified three-point data in the sources I found.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-11, weight 230 to 236 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a versatile forward or centre who can pass, rebound and protect the rim. His 2026-27 season as a senior will decide whether his NBA stock rises.

Intangibles
Played at the NBA Global Academy in Australia, the same programme as Josh Giddey and Patty Mills. Described by Florida as a national champion and a starter for a team with a strong culture.

Summary and Projection
A high-IQ forward with a proven record of production. He is a likely first-round pick if he continues his improvement as a senior.

Sources: Florida athletics roster; OnlyGators; ESPN; RotoWire; Stat Sniper; Proballers.

name: Hugo Yimga Moukouri
video_note:
Overview
French forward who joined Nanterre 92 in Betclic Élite (France’s top men’s league, sometimes listed as LNB Élite) at age 16. He was named the league’s Best Young Player for 2025-26 at age 17. He has represented France at youth level, including the FIBA U17 World Cup and the 2025 U18 EuroBasket.

Current Stats (2025-26 Nanterre, Betclic Élite)
Points 8.9, rebounds 3.8, 18 minutes a game.
Field goal 61.4%, three-point 40.5%.
Sources also give national-league averages of about 10.4 points and 5.4 rebounds, so treat the exact figures as approximate.
2026-27 Nanterre: two games, 9.0 points and 5.5 rebounds a game.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Shooting efficiency: 61.4% from the field and 40.5% from three for a teenager in the French top flight.
Size: listed at 6-8 (203 cm) and 219 lbs for a wing.
Early experience: playing professional minutes at age 16 and 17.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)
Role and minutes: 18 minutes a game limits his development and makes his data harder to judge.
Physicality: at 219 lbs, he will need to add strength to guard grown men in European and NBA-style matchups.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-8 (203 cm), weight 219 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a wing who can shoot and make plays. Scouts in France treat him as one of the country’s top young prospects.

Intangibles
At 17 he was described as one of the league’s great revelations, and coach Julien Mahé spoke highly of him when he joined the club.

Summary and Projection
A young, efficient French prospect who has already shown he can produce in a top professional league. Minutes and physical development are the next steps.

Sources: Wikipedia (LNB Élite and player page); LNB.fr; RealGM; Bebasket; EuroBasket.com; Flashscore.

name: Mackenzie Mgbako
video_note:
Overview
Franklin, New Jersey, native and Roselle Catholic graduate. 2023 McDonald’s All-American and Big Ten co-Freshman of the Year at Indiana. Transferred to Texas A&M and played only seven games in 2025-26 before a foot injury ended his season. He is planning to return to Texas A&M for 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Texas A&M, 7 games)
Points 10.4, rebounds 4.9, assists 1.3, steals 0.6, blocks 0.1.
Minutes 18.7 a game.
Field goal 39.0%, three-point 34.3%, free throw 88.2%.
Foot injury in December 2025 ended his season early.

Previous seasons at Indiana:
2023-24 (freshman): 12.2 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.2 turnovers, 33 games, 27 minutes.
2024-25 (sophomore): 12.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 32 games, 25 minutes.
Career high: 31 points against SIU Edwardsville.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Scoring: 12.2 points a game at Indiana twice, and 10.4 points in limited minutes at A&M.
Free throws: 88.2% in 2025-26, and 82% for his career.
Size and length: 6-9, 225 lbs.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Efficiency: 39% from the field across his career, and 34% from three.
Availability: only seven games in 2025-26 because of injury.
Playmaking: 1.3 assists a game is limited for a forward.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-9, weight 225 lbs. No verified testing data beyond a G League Elite Camp appearance in 2025, where he averaged 20.5 points in two games.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a versatile wing-forward who can score from multiple levels. A healthy 2026-27 season at Texas A&M would show whether he can be an efficient regular.

Intangibles
Father-led family background in New Jersey basketball. Earlier coverage described him as a projected NBA draft pick.

Summary and Projection
A talented, efficient scorer with a limited recent sample. His health and field goal percentage in 2026-27 will decide his projection.

Sources: Texas A&M athletics roster; RealGM; RotoWire; ESPN; SI; Stat Sniper.

name: Na'jai Hines
video_note:
Overview
Plainfield, New Jersey, native, ranked No. 1 player in New Jersey in the 2025 class by 247Sports. Freshman at Seton Hall in 2025-26, where he came off the bench. He transferred to UConn for 2026-27 and is expected to be a starter.

Current Stats (2025-26 Seton Hall, freshman season, 31 to 33 games, mostly off the bench)
Points 6.4 to 6.5, rebounds 5.5 to 5.8, assists 0.6 to 0.7, steals 0.3 to 0.4, blocks 2.2 to 2.3.
Minutes about 18 a game.
Field goal 60.2%, free throw 69%.
Led the Big East in blocks per game (2.2).
Scored in double figures 11 times and had four double-doubles.
Absences: missed games with an ankle issue and an illness.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Rim protection: 2.2 blocks a game, the Big East’s best.
Efficiency: 60.2% from the field.
Rebounding: 5.5 a game in limited minutes.
Senior-year production: 18.8 points, 16.9 rebounds and 3.5 blocks in high school, with a double-double in every game.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Playmaking and offence: 0.6 assists a game and little offensive role so far.
Conditioning and weight: he weighed about 278 lbs during much of 2025-26 and has since lost about 10 lbs.
Free throws: 69% is below what is expected from a big.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-10 to 6-11 (sources differ), weight 265 to 278 lbs. No verified testing data. Summer weight loss may affect mobility.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a traditional rim-protecting centre. His role at UConn will depend on how far his weight loss improves his mobility and conditioning.

Intangibles
One of 14 children, a two-sport athlete who also received football offers as a tight end. He is studying sports media. Nicknamed “Big Jah” and “Terminator.”

Summary and Projection
A shot-blocking centre with a clear defensive identity but a limited offensive profile so far. His 2026-27 role will show whether he can grow beyond defence.

Sources: UConn athletics roster; Seton Hall roster; RotoWire; Stat Sniper; CBS Sports.

name: Milan Momcilovic
video_note:
Overview
Pewaukee, Wisconsin, native and Iowa State forward who led the nation in three-point shooting in 2025-26. Second-team All-Big 12. He declared for the NBA draft, withdrew, and committed to Kentucky as a transfer for 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Iowa State, 37 games, 30.5 minutes)
Points 16.9, rebounds 3.1.
Three-point 48.7% on 7.5 attempts a game, the best in the NCAA.
Made at least five threes in ten games, including eight in one Big 12 Tournament game against Arizona.
Season high: 34 points with eight threes at Cincinnati.
Iowa State went 29-8 and reached the Sweet 16.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Shooting: NCAA-best 48.7% from three.
Two-way play: described by SI as having elite two-way skills, with the size and athleticism to guard forwards on the perimeter.
Basketball IQ: scouts praise his high IQ on offence.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)
Rebounding: 3.1 a game is low for a 6-8 forward.
Playmaking and creation: his offence is mostly catch-and-shoot, so his ability to create off the dribble is unproven.
Consistency: some games produced far fewer points, including a 2-of-6 three-point game during a 20-point scoring stretch.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-8 (ESPN and Kentucky lists) or 6-9 (Kentucky’s earlier roster), weight 220 to 225 lbs. Described as athletic enough to defend on the perimeter. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a three-and-D wing who can stretch the floor. Scouts see him as a second-round pick with a clear role as a shooter.

Intangibles
High basketball IQ, and described as a competitor who takes big shots. Nicknamed “MoneyMil” and “Serbian Sniper”. Favourite player is Stephen Curry.

Summary and Projection
One of the best shooters in college basketball, with the role and size to play at the next level. Rebounding and creating off the dribble are the next steps.

Sources: Kentucky athletics roster; Iowa State coverage (AP, ESPN); SI; Wikipedia; Stat Sniper; Action News Jax (AP).

name: Motiejus Krivas
video_note:
Overview
Lithuanian centre from Šiauliai, who came through Kaunas Žalgiris II and joined Arizona in 2023. He was a First Team All-Big 12 and Big 12 All-Defensive Team selection in 2025-26, and a late first-round prospect who considered the 2026 NBA Draft before returning for his senior season.

Current Stats (2025-26 Arizona, junior season)
Points 10.4 (some sources say 10.5), rebounds 8.2, assists 1.1, blocks 1.9 (73 total, 17th nationally).
Minutes 25.3 a game.
Field goal 56.9%.
Opponents shot 36.7% when he was on the court, the lowest in the country according to CBB Analytics.
Season high: 15 rebounds and six blocks at Kansas.
Freshman season (2023-24): 5.4 points and 4.2 rebounds in 36 games off the bench.
Missed most of 2024-25 with a lower-leg injury and surgery.
2026-27 college: season not started.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Rim protection: 1.9 blocks a game, and the lowest opponent field goal percentage in the country.
Rebounding: 8.2 a game as a junior, second on the team behind a senior.
Efficiency: 56.9% from the field.
Size and mobility: 7-2 with the foot speed and length to defend in space.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)
Offence: mostly finishing and post play, with a developing mid-range game.
Injury history: the 2024-25 lower-leg injury cost him most of a season.
Free throws: career 77.8% as a freshman, so consistency at the line is still a question.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 7-2, weight 255 to 260 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a rim-protecting centre who defends and rebounds. Another season could move him into the first round.

Intangibles
Played for Lithuania at FIBA U20 level, including the 2023 European Championship. Named to the all-tournament team at the ANGT in 2022.

Summary and Projection
One of the best defensive bigs in college basketball and a first-round candidate for 2027. His offence is the main development area.

Sources: Arizona athletics roster; AP; RotoWire; Stat Sniper; Arizona Sports.

name: Amani Hansberry
video_note:
Overview
Silver Spring, Maryland native from Mount Saint Joseph in Baltimore. Started at Illinois, transferred to West Virginia, then to Virginia Tech for 2025-26. Junior in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Virginia Tech, 30 games, 18 to 22 starts)
Points 14.3, rebounds 7.4, assists 2.4, steals about 1.0.
Minutes 30.7 a game.
Field goal 49.2%, three-point 35.4%, free throw 73.6%.
Season high: 17 points, 15 rebounds, two blocks and two steals in a triple-overtime win over Virginia.
Season high: 18 points and six assists against Western Carolina.

Previous seasons (West Virginia, 2024-25): 9.8 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.4 assists in 31 games, 24 starts.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Rebounding: 7.4 a game for a 6-8 forward.
Efficiency: 49.2% from the field and 35.4% from three.
Versatility: he has shown he can play multiple frontcourt roles, and he has a double-double in several games.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Free throws: 73.6% is below what is needed for a primary scorer.
Turnovers: about 3 a game, which is high for his assist total.
Availability: he was listed on injury reports during the season, and a lower-body injury cost him games at West Virginia.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-8, weight 240 lbs. No verified testing data.

Projects as a physical forward who can rebound and score inside. Scouts would want to see more consistency as a playmaker and shooter.

Son of Paul and Angela Hansberry. Has been a transfer twice, so his adaptability has been tested.

Summary and Projection
A productive, physical forward with strong rebounding and efficient shooting. Consistency and health are the main points to watch in his final season.

Sources: Virginia Tech roster (hokiesports.com); ProBallers; RotoWire; Stat Sniper; Lines.

name: Jeremy Fears Jr.
video_note:
Overview
Joliet, Illinois native and La Lumiere graduate. Redshirt sophomore point guard, Wooden Award All-American selection and captain, who led Michigan State in scoring and set the school’s assist record. He withdrew from the 2026 NBA Draft and is returning for 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Michigan State, 35 games)
Points 15.2 to 15.7, rebounds 2.4, assists 9.4 (school record 328 total), steals 1.1 to 1.3.
Minutes 32.4 a game.
Field goal 43.1%, three-point 32.1%, free throw 88.5%.
Season highs include 26 points against Illinois and 22 against Duke-area opponents earlier in the year.
Michigan State went 27-8 and 15-5 in the Big Ten.
Previous season (2024-25): 7.2 points, 5.4 assists, 39.7% from the field.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Playmaking: 9.4 assists a game is one of the best numbers in the country.
Scoring improvement: from 7.2 points to 15.2 in one year.
Free throws: 88.5% is elite for a guard.
Basketball IQ: scouts describe him as one of the best playmakers in the country, with control over tempo.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)
Shooting efficiency: 43.1% from the field and 32.1% from three. The Michigan State staff want him closer to 40% from the field.
Turnovers: about 2.4 a game, which is high for a point guard.
Size: 6-2, 190 lbs, which is a concern for defending bigger guards.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-2, weight 180 to 190 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a lead point guard who can run an offence and score when needed. Scouts see him as a top-two-round pick with more upside if he improves his shooting.

Intangibles
Captain and Wooden Award All-American. Michigan State’s first Wooden All-American since Cassius Winston.

Summary and Projection
One of the best passers in college basketball and a major piece of Michigan State’s return. Shooting efficiency will decide whether he becomes a first-round player.

Sources: Michigan State athletics release; RotoWire; ESPN; Stat Sniper; SI; Spartan Avenue.

name: Ruben Prey
video_note:
Overview
Lisbon, Portugal native who came through Joventut Badalona in Spain’s ACB. Joined St. John’s and was a rotation big in 2025-26. Sophomore in 2025-26 and junior in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 St. John’s, 37 games, one start)
Points 4.3, rebounds 2.1, assists 0.8, blocks 0.7, steals 0.4.
Minutes about 10.7 a game.
Field goal 50.5%, three-point 62.5% (15 of 24), free throw 67.2%.
Shot 88.9% from the field in the three NCAA Tournament games, including 12 points against Duke in the Sweet 16.
Previous season (2024-25): 1.6 points and 1.5 rebounds in 33 games.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)
Shooting: 62.5% from three on a small sample, and he scored in double figures in the tournament.
Size: 6-11, 230 lbs, with a frame to play in the post.
Improvement: his scoring went from 1.6 points to 4.3 in one year.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats)
Playing time: 10.7 minutes a game limits how much his numbers show.
Rebounding and defence: 2.1 rebounds and 0.7 blocks a game are modest for a 6-11 big.
Shot volume: his three-point sample is small, so the 62.5% should not be read as proven.

Physical and Athletic Profile
Height 6-11, weight 230 lbs. No verified testing data.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a reserve big who can stretch the floor. With Zuby Ejiofor graduating, he is the main candidate for a bigger role in 2026-27.

Intangibles
Son of Catrin Prey and David Pinto. Played in Spain’s youth system before arriving in the US.

Summary and Projection
A developing big whose strongest number is a small sample of three-point shooting. A bigger role in 2026-27 would show whether his growth continues.

Sources: St. John’s athletics roster; RealGM; RotoWire; Stat Sniper; Lines.

name: Tahaad Pettiford
video_note:
Overview
Jersey City, New Jersey native and 2024 McDonald’s All-American from Hudson Catholic. SEC All-Freshman in 2024. Sophomore point guard at Auburn in 2025-26, and returning for a third season in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Auburn, sophomore season, 38 games, 36 starts)
Points 15.4 to 15.6, rebounds 3.0, assists 3.8, steals 1.1, blocks 0.6.
Minutes 32.3 a game.
Field goal 39.3%, three-point 29.0%, free throw 82.5%.

name: Terrance Arceneaux
video_note:
Overview
Jersey City, New Jersey native and 2024 McDonald’s All-American from Hudson Catholic. SEC All-Freshman in 2024. Sophomore point guard at Auburn in 2025-26, returning for a third season in 2026-27.

Current Stats (2025-26 Auburn, sophomore season, 38 games, 36 starts)
15.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.6 blocks in 32.3 minutes per game. Shot 39.3% from the field, 29.0% from three and 82.5% from the free-throw line. Led the Players Era Festival in scoring at 22.3 points per game and led Auburn with 145 assists.

Previous season, 2024-25: 11.6 points, 2.2 rebounds and 3.0 assists in 38 games, with one start.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)

Scoring: Averaged 15.4 points as a sophomore starter and scored 585 points across the season, ranking 15th on Auburn’s single-season scoring list.

Free throws: 82.5% from the line, a strong indicator of touch and ability to convert under pressure.

Quickness and transition: Described as explosive and effective in fast-paced situations, with the profile of a guard who can create early offense.

Shot creation: His scoring jump from 11.6 to 15.4 points per game came while moving into a full-time starting role, suggesting he can carry more offensive responsibility.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)

Efficiency: 39.3% from the field and 29.0% from three are below the level you want from a lead guard, especially after shooting 42.1% from the field and 36.6% from three as a freshman.

Size: Listed at 6-1 and around 169-170 pounds, which is light for an SEC point guard and could create finishing and defensive concerns against bigger backcourts.

Turnovers and playmaking: He averaged 3.8 assists and 2.2 turnovers, so the assist-to-turnover ratio is positive, but his decision-making in half-court settings still needs closer film review.

Three-point consistency: The drop from 36.6% to 29.0% is the main development question; improving shot selection and catch-and-shoot reliability would materially raise his ceiling.

Physical and Athletic Profile
6-1, approximately 169-170 pounds. No verified wingspan, vertical or combine-style testing data included here. His quickness, burst and ability to play at speed appear to be core athletic strengths, but his frame will need to hold up against physical college and professional guards.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a scoring point guard who can attack in transition, generate his own shot and provide secondary playmaking. His best fit is likely as a lead or combo guard allowed to hunt offense, ideally alongside a bigger defensive guard and spacing bigs. His shooting efficiency and size will ultimately determine whether he projects as a high-level starter or a microwave scoring reserve.

Intangibles
Auburn’s seventh-ever McDonald’s All-American. Bruce Pearl has described him as one of the team’s key players, and he returned for a third college season rather than leaving after his sophomore year.

Summary and Projection
A talented, quick scoring guard with real shot-making ability, free-throw touch and transition juice, but limited size and inconsistent shooting efficiency. A stronger three-point season in 2026-27, combined with improved physical strength and half-court decision-making, would define his draft trajectory and long-term role.

Sources: Auburn athletics roster; ESPN; Wikipedia; RotoWire; Sportskeeda; Yahoo Sports; 247Sports.

name: Jalil Bethea
video_note:

Current Stats (2025-26 Alabama, sophomore season, 26 games)
3.9 points, 1.7 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 7.9 minutes per game. Shot 37.5% from the field, 31.4% from three and 80.6% from the free-throw line.

Previous season, 2024-25: 7.1 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 31 games.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)

Free-throw touch: 80.6% from the line supports legitimate shooting feel.

Perimeter shooting potential: 31.4% from three on limited volume, with prior shooting pedigree suggesting room to develop into a reliable catch-and-shoot wing.

Size for a guard: Listed at 6-5, 192 pounds, giving him useful wing dimensions.

Scoring flashes: Scored a career-high 21 points against UTSA, showing he can heat up when given opportunity.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)

Efficiency: 37.5% from the field and 31.4% from three need to rise for him to earn a bigger role.

Playmaking: 0.5 assists per game shows very little creation or connective playmaking in his current role.

Opportunity: His minutes fell sharply from 19.0 to 7.9 per game, so he needs to convert limited chances into consistent production.

Physical and Athletic Profile
6-5, approximately 192 pounds. No verified athletic testing data included here. His size is a real positive for a shooting-guard projection.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a wing scorer and spot-up threat rather than a primary creator. Best fit is in a spaced, fast system where he can attack closeouts, make open threes and defend multiple perimeter positions.

Intangibles
Former high-major recruit with a strong developmental pedigree, but his sophomore season suggests he needs a clearer role and more consistent confidence.

Summary and Projection
A tools-based wing with shooting touch and size, but currently unproven as an efficient, high-minutes contributor. His development depends on turning shooting feel into consistent three-point production and adding simple playmaking.

Sources: Alabama athletics; ESPN; USbasket.

name: DJ Wagner
video_note:

Former Kentucky guard who transferred to Arkansas and played his junior season there in 2025-26. A former high-profile recruit with NBA lineage, now projecting as a backup/rotation guard rather than a high-usage lead creator.

Current Stats (2025-26 Arkansas, junior season, 35 games, 19 starts)
7.4 points, 1.6 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.3 blocks in 23.6 minutes per game. Shot 42.9% from the field, 34.6% from three and 72.4% from the free-throw line.

Efficiency improvement: Career-best 42.9% from the field and 34.6% from three.

Ball security: 85 assists against only 23 turnovers, an excellent 3.7:1 assist-to-turnover ratio.

Size for a guard: 6-4, approximately 194 pounds, giving him the frame to play either backcourt spot.

Experience: Three seasons of high-major basketball with prior starting experience at Kentucky and Arkansas.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)

Creation load: His scoring and assist numbers dropped sharply from his Kentucky seasons, indicating a more limited on-ball role.

Free throws: 72.4% is below the standard for a guard with his experience.

Athletic separation: His modest rebounding and steal rates suggest he is not an elite athlete or high-impact defender; film is needed to confirm his ability to create against length.

Physical and Athletic Profile
6-4, approximately 194 pounds. Solid size for a combo guard, though his current production profile suggests he is more of a controlled connector than an explosive athlete.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a secondary ball-handler, low-mistake connector and spot-up threat. Best fit is next to a primary creator, where he can defend a bigger guard, make open shots and keep the offense organised.

Intangibles
Strong basketball background and high-major experience, with a clear ability to fit into a structured system rather than force the action.

Summary and Projection
A experienced, low-turnover combo guard whose shooting improved but whose creation and athletic upside remain limited. His path is as a reliable depth guard who can stabilise a second unit, not currently a lead initiator.

Sources: Arkansas/Maryland athletics; ESPN; CBS Sports; RotoWire; Scout Basketball.

name: Cameron Houindo
video_note:
Overview
French 2008-born forward who moved from Pôle France to Cedevita Olimpija in Ljubljana in summer 2025. He is one of the leading European prospects in his age group and won FIBA U16 EuroBasket MVP in 2024 while leading France to the title.

Current Stats (2025-26 Cedevita Olimpija)
In senior ABA League action, he appeared in limited minutes and averaged roughly 2.6 points and 1.5 rebounds per game.

In EuroCup/ABA senior competition, he played five games at 9.3 minutes per game, averaging 0.8 points, 0.6 rebounds and 1.0 assist.

At youth level, he was far more productive: 22.0 points and 7.5 rebounds per game in the EuroLeague NextGen Ulm Qualifier, winning tournament MVP, then 21.0 points and 9.7 rebounds at the Finals in Athens.

Strengths (verified stats and inference from published scouting)

Youth-level scoring: 33 points in an ANGT game against U18 EA7 Emporio Armani Milan shows real scoring upside for his age.

Rebounding and motor: 9.7 rebounds per game at the NextGen Finals suggests he can impact the game physically against peers.

Size and mobility: Listed at 206 cm, with a profile built around explosiveness and frontcourt versatility.

International pedigree: FIBA U16 EuroBasket MVP and a key role in France’s 2024 title run.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)

Senior-level adjustment: His senior minutes and production remain limited, so he must prove his youth dominance translates against stronger, older competition.

Efficiency: His limited senior sample includes poor shooting numbers, including 20% from the field in EuroCup/ABA play.

Physical development: Born in 2008, he is still early in his strength and maturity curve.

Physical and Athletic Profile
206 cm, born January 2008. A long, athletic forward with encouraging mobility and explosive traits, but still developing physically.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a mobile, energetic forward who can rebound, finish in transition and develop into a multi-position defender. Best fit is a developmental European environment where he can earn minutes gradually rather than being forced into a major senior role too early.

Intangibles
His youth accolades and tournament MVP performances show a high competitive level, but his current professional role is still very small.

Summary and Projection
A high-upside French forward with strong youth production, athleticism and international pedigree, but very limited senior-level evidence. His development depends on adding strength, improving efficiency and earning consistent professional minutes.

Sources: Cedevita Olimpija; ABA League; RealGM; Wikipedia; BeBasket; Proballers.

name: Pavle Backo
video_note:

Serbian 2007-born big man playing for Mega Basket in the ABA League system. He has also represented Serbia at U18 level and has strong youth-production numbers.

In ABA League 2026-27 action, he averaged 7.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 21 minutes across two games, shooting 38.5% from the field.

In EuroBasket U18 play, he averaged 16.7 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.2 blocks and 0.5 assists in 20.9 minutes over six games, shooting 61.3% from the field, 46.2% from three and 94.7% from the line.

Interior scoring: 61.3% shooting and 65.3% on two-point attempts at U18 level show strong finishing around the basket.

Free-throw shooting: 94.7% from the line in U18 play is an unusually strong indicator of touch for a young center.

Three-point potential: 46.2% from three on 2.2 attempts per game at U18 level suggests stretch-big potential, though the sample is small.

** rim protection:** 1.2 blocks per game in U18 competition supports a basic protective presence.

Turnovers: 3.2 turnovers against 0.5 assists at U18 level is a major concern for a big man.

Senior-level efficiency: His limited ABA sample shows 38.5% shooting, so he must prove his youth-level finishing translates.

Physical readiness: At 2.10 metres and born in 2007, he is still developing the strength needed for regular senior competition.

Physical and Athletic Profile
2.10 metres, born November 2007. A modern-size center with encouraging shooting indicators, but still early in his physical development.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a skilled stretch center who can finish inside, space the floor and protect the rim. Best fit is in a developmental European environment before any NBA evaluation becomes serious.

Intangibles
His U18 production and shooting numbers are encouraging, but the large turnover rate and limited senior minutes mean his readiness is still uncertain.

Summary and Projection
A intriguing young Serbian center with size, touch and stretch potential, but major decision-making and physical-development questions. He is a long-term developmental prospect rather than an immediate impact player.

Sources: ABA League; RealGM; Scout Basketball; BeBasketball.

name: Jamari Phillips
video_note:

Sophomore shooting guard at Oregon who spent two quiet seasons with the Ducks before entering the transfer portal.

2.7 points, 0.9 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 11.4 minutes per game. Shot 31.5% from the field, 29.5% from three and 83.3% from the free-throw line.

Free-throw touch: 83.3% from the line supports real shooting mechanics and touch.

Efficiency: 31.5% from the field and 29.5% from three are well below the level needed for a shooting-guard role.

Production: 2.7 points and 0.5 assists in 11.4 minutes show he has not yet translated his shooting potential into consistent college impact.

No verified height, weight or athletic testing data included here. His profile is currently defined more by shooting potential than by measurable physical tools.

Projects as a movement shooter and low-usage wing. Best fit is a system that gives him simple catch-and-shoot chances while hiding him from heavy creation duties.

Intangibles
He has kept a professional shooting stroke and free-throw number despite limited minutes, which suggests some underlying skill, but his overall college impact has been minimal.

A developmental shooter whose college production has not matched his pre-college reputation. He needs a fresh role, improved shot selection and much better efficiency to become a rotation-level guard.

name: Rueben Chinyelu

11.7 points, 11.8 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.7 steals in 24.4 minutes per game. Shot 60.7% from the field, 68.5% from the free-throw line and attempted only two threes.

Second-chance impact: His offensive-rebounding volume creates extra possessions and easy scoring chances.

Durability and experience: Three college seasons and a growing starting role show continued physical and tactical development.

Range: Essentially no three-point threat, with only two career attempts.

Playmaking: 0.6 assists per game shows limited passing or hub potential.

Fouls: 3.0 personal fouls per game in 24.4 minutes is a concern for a starting center.

Defensive versatility: His profile suggests a traditional, physical interior defender rather than a switchable modern big; film is needed to confirm lateral movement.

No verified height, weight, wingspan or testing data included here. His statistical profile points to a strong, physical, possession-controlling center.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a traditional rebounding and finishing center. Best fit is next to spacing bigs and creators, where he can screen, roll, clean the glass and defend the paint.

Intangibles
His jump from 6.0 to 11.7 points and 6.6 to 11.8 rebounds shows a major year-over-year leap in role and production.

Summary and Projection
A high-level college rebounder and efficient rim finisher, but a limited modern offensive big. His professional ceiling depends on defensive mobility, foul control and whether he can add any credible shooting or passing.

Sources: Florida athletics via ESPN; CBS Sports; RotoWire; Gaussian Hoops.

name: Moustapha Thiam
video_note:

Sophomore center at Cincinnati who built on a productive freshman season with a larger role in 2025-26. A rim-protecting, efficient interior scorer with some perimeter shooting potential.

Current Stats (2025-26 Cincinnati, sophomore season, 31 games)
12.8 points, 7.1 rebounds, 0.5 assists, 1.6 blocks and 0.8 steals in 27.2 minutes per game. Shot 52.5% from the field, 28.8% from three and 63.3% from the free-throw line.

Rim protection: 1.6 blocks per game, following 2.6 as a freshman, shows a consistent shot-blocking presence.

Interior efficiency: 52.5% from the field supports reliable finishing near the basket.

Perimeter curiosity: 28.8% from three is not efficient yet, but the fact he takes threes gives him developmental stretch potential.

Defensive activity: 0.8 steals and 1.6 blocks suggest he can impact possessions beyond the box score.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)

Free throws: 63.3% from the line is a concern for a center with shooting ambitions.

Three-point efficiency: 28.8% needs major improvement before defences genuinely respect him outside.

Playmaking: 0.5 assists per game shows very little passing value.

Foul discipline: 2.0 fouls in 27.2 minutes is manageable but needs to stay controlled as his role grows.

Physical and Athletic Profile
No verified height, weight, wingspan or testing data included here. His statistical profile points to a long, active, shot-blocking center.

Projects as a defensive anchor and vertical-spacing big. Best fit is with guards who can create and wings who can space the floor, allowing him to protect the rim, roll hard and occasionally pop.

Intangibles
He maintained strong block numbers while increasing his scoring role, which is a positive sign for his defensive foundation.

Summary and Projection
A legitimate rim protector with efficient interior scoring and developmental shooting upside. His ceiling depends on improving free throws, three-point accuracy and passing; his floor is as a defensive-minded backup center.

Sources: Cincinnati athletics via ESPN; CBS Sports; RotoWire; 247Sports.

name: Sayon Keita
video_note:

Mali-born, Spain-developed freshman center at North Carolina, previously with FC Barcelona. He reclassified into the 2026 class and committed to UNC in April 2026.

Current Stats (2025-26 FC Barcelona)
In six EuroLeague games, he averaged 2.5 points, 1.5 rebounds, 0.5 steals and 0.2 blocks in 8.6 minutes per game, shooting 58.3% from the field.

In Spanish league play, he averaged 0.9 points and 1.3 rebounds in 5.5 minutes across nine games.

Elite length: Measured 6-foot-10¾ with a 7-foot-7 wingspan and 9-foot-4½ standing reach at the NBPA Top 100 Camp.

Rim protection: Averaged 3.2 blocks per game at a major U.S. high-school camp and 4.0 blocks per game at the NBA Academy Games.

Mobility: Scouts describe him as a big mover with quick feet, the ability to run the floor, defend ball screens in multiple ways and potentially switch.

Finishing and lob threat: A bouncy finisher who separates quickly as a roller and projects as a lob target.

Areas for Improvement (verified stats and inference)

Strength: His frame is still undeveloped, and physicality against older college bigs is viewed as his biggest immediate challenge.

Offensive polish: His senior-level scoring is minimal, and he remains largely a finisher rather than a self-creator.

Free throws: Limited senior sample shows 50% from the line in EuroLeague and 33.3% in Spanish league play.

Experience: Only 15 senior appearances across EuroLeague and Spanish league play, so his college readiness is still uncertain.

Physical and Athletic Profile
7-0, approximately 205-215 pounds, with a reported 7-foot-5 to 7-foot-7 wingspan. Exceptional length, mobility and defensive tools for his age.

Playstyle and Fit
Projects as a long, active rim protector, vertical spacer and lob finisher. Best fit is a system that lets him screen, roll, protect the paint and defend in space while he adds strength and offensive skill.

Intangibles
Defensive MVP at a major invitational camp and strong showings at the NBA Academy Games and EuroLeague NextGen suggest high-level competitive instincts.

Summary and Projection
A high-upside, long-term developmental center with rare length, mobility and rim-protection instincts. His NBA ceiling is significant, but he is raw, light and still needs to prove he can handle physical college competition.

Sources: ESPN; 247Sports; Chapelboro; USA Today; ShamSports; RotoWire.

name: Silas Demary Jr.

Senior guard at UConn who previously played at Georgia. A experienced, high-assist point guard with strong shooting numbers and a clear connector profile.

Current Stats (2025-26 UConn, senior season, 39 games)
10.1 points, 4.5 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 1.6 steals and 0.3 blocks in 28.4 minutes per game. Shot 44.6% from the field, 38.5% from three and 80.1% from the free-throw line.

Playmaking: 5.9 assists per game ranks among the better college guard marks, with a strong 2.7:1 assist-to-turnover ratio.

Shooting: 38.5% from three and 80.1% from the line support a legitimate spacing threat.

Efficiency: 44.6% from the field is a clear improvement from 39.6% the previous season.

Defense: 1.6 steals per game suggests active hands and useful perimeter defensive engagement.

No verified height, weight, wingspan or testing data included here. His profile is built around feel, decision-making, shooting and defensive activity rather than overwhelming physical tools.

Projects as a low-mistake, pass-first point guard who can shoot, defend his position and run an offence. Best fit is next to a scoring guard or wing, where he can organise the offence without needing to carry the scoring load.

Intangibles
Three seasons of college experience, steady assist production and improved efficiency point to a mature, system-friendly guard.

Summary and Projection
A reliable, experienced combo/point guard with strong passing, shooting and defensive activity. His professional ceiling depends on whether he can create more efficiently against high-level athletes, but his floor is as a steady backup or rotation guard.

Sources: UConn athletics via ESPN; CBS Sports; FOX Sports.
